📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 maintains the fast, versatile ride the line is known for while adding a little more comfort, making it a successful if minor update on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s one of the best fast trainers available and if you’ve loved past models, the Speed 6 is unlikely to disappoint, but there are some fantastic alternatives to consider too.

Stable and comfortable at easy paces.

According to recent reports, why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed has been one of the most influential running shoes of recent years, setting the template for fast training sneakers that uses some of the materials and tech from top carbon plate racers.

With the line proving so successful, Saucony has been reluctant to change much about the shoe over the five generations to date, and even though the Endorphin Speed 6 is the biggest enhancement yet thanks to a new midsole foam, it mostly retains the same ride feel as past models.

In a recent development, I’ve reviewed every model of the Endorphin Speed and I’ve always been a big fan. While that’s still true with the Speed 6, this category contains some of the best running shoes available, and there are some lighter, bouncier fast trainers I rate very highly, like the Newly introduced Balance SC Rebel v1 and Dynafish Xiaonian.

The Saucony Endorphin Speed 6 costs $180 in the U.S. and £180 in the U.K., which is a $5 price rise on the Endorphin Speed 5. It’s an expensive shoe, though not out of line with other plated trainers like the Hoka Mach X3 and Fresh Balance SC Rebel v1.

Right now the Saucony Endorphin Speed 5 is widely reduced, dropping to $104 on Amazon in the Black Friday sales, which is a factor to consider when weighing up buying the Speed.

The Endorphin Speed 6 is at the moment available in five colors in the women’s shoe, and four colors in the men’s, including the white and yellow design I tested.

There is a wide version of the shoe available, though I found that the standard one fit me well in my normal running shoe size, the same size I’ve used with all past models of the shoe.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Saucony has added 2mm of foam to the midsole of the Endorphin Speed 6, which has a stack height of 38mm at the heel and 30mm at the forefoot, maintaining the 8mm drop of past models.

It weighs in at 8.5oz, which is 0.5oz lighter than the Endorphin Speed 5 in my size, a welcome drop for a speed-focused shoe.

The Endorphin Speed 6 has a simple mesh upper that has a little bit of padding around the tongue and collar, but mostly focuses on being lightweight and breathable.

It’s my preferred kind of upper on any shoe, since it’s not oppressively padded on the tongue or overly stiff around the heel, and I found the fit comfortable and secure throughout all my runs.

The Endorphin Speed 6’s main changes are in the midsole, which is made from a new foam called PWRRUN PBX, which is meant to be lighter and bouncier than the PWRRUN PB that has been used on all past models of the shoe.

There’s also the higher stack and a redesigned nylon plate in the midsole, which aims to create a smoother, faster ride, with the Speedroll rocker on the shoe also contributing to this.

The changes to the midsole are noticeable on the run, though not as dramatically as I expected when looking at the spec sheet for the Speed 6.

Rubber is used sparingly on the bottom of the Speed 6 to keep the weight down, but patches cover the forefoot and heel of the shoe, and in my experience Saucony’s pelletized midsole foams are durable even when the foam is exposed on the bottom of a shoe.

Grip hasn’t always been a positive feature on the Speed line, but the Speed 6 provided me with reliable traction in wet conditions on both the road and the track during my testing.

After the very pleasant surprise of the original Endorphin Speed, which I ran over 300 miles in, I’ve found that the line has delivered a reliably similar experience with all of the models since.

There have been updates to make it more stable and comfortable, but ultimately all five versions of the Speed to date have had a smooth, fast and versatile ride feel.

This is still true of the Endorphin Speed 6 for me, and while that’s mostly a positive in that it performed well across a variety of runs in my testing, some might have hoped for a bigger change to challenge rivals like the SC Rebel v1 and cheaper, lighter options like the Adidas Adizero Evo SL and Dynafish Xiaonian.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

I used the shoe for a couple of easy runs, two progression runs moving from easy to tempo pace, and a threshold track workout running 4 x 8min reps, and it felt great throughout.

The rockered midsole pushes you smoothly through your footstrike, and while the midsole foam isn’t as soft and springy as some, it does give a good amount of energy return off the toes.

I also found the Speed 6 to be quite stable and comfortable for easy runs, which is not always the case with plated trainers like this. I could happily use it for pretty much any kind of run, though it’s not as fast as a true carbon plate racer, or as comfortable as a max-cushioned cruiser.

To compare it directly to the Endorphin Speed 5 I did a short run wearing both shoes, and while the Speed 6 is a little bouncier and more comfortable, especially under the forefoot, I still felt the two shoes had a similar ride feel.

According to recent reports, the Speed 6 is still a bit firmer than most super-trainers, and not as comfortable as more cushioned shoes under the toes. Some will like this more direct ride feel, but I appreciate the extra softness and bounce of a shoe like the SC Rebel v1.

If you’re a long term fan of the Endorphin Speed line the Speed 6 will be a winner. It’s a mild improvement on the previous models with extra cushion and bounce, and delivers the versatile performance you expect from the line.

There is certainly a case for getting the Speed 5 instead in sales in my opinion, but the Speed 6 is a slightly better shoe overall and a successful update.

The Speed line has been faced with increasingly fierce competition in recent years, and I don’t think the Speed 6 does much to change the equation on this front.

If you want a lighter, bouncier fast trainer, the Latest Balance SC Rebel v1 would be my pick, while plate-free shoes like the Adidas Evo SL, Dyanfish Xiaonian and the new 361° Mega 3 Pro all offer fast, fun rides at a lower price.

As someone who would always have had the Endorphin Speed in my own rotation through the first few models, I’ve now moved on to shoes like this myself. Even though the Speed 6 is just as good as past models, I personally like the springier ride available in fast trainers.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Lifehacker Senior Health Editor Beth Skwarecki ran the Forerunner 265 through its paces for us, and says the device completely transformed her runs.
  • The Forerunner 265 is built for runners who want more training data than a general fitness or lifestyle watch offers.

If you’re an avid runner, fitness watch features like step and heart rate tracking are just the beginning, and Garmin is leading the charge when it comes to more advanced, comprehensive metrics. The right running watch can be more than a gadget, but an essential training tool—and right now, one of the best is $150 cheaper thanks to Amazon’s early Black Friday sale. The Garmin Forerunner 265 is now 33% off, taking it down to $309.99 (originally $459.99).

Lifehacker Senior Health Editor Beth Skwarecki ran the Forerunner 265 through its paces for us, and says the device completely transformed her runs. The 46mm watch is the larger counterpart to the 42mm 265S (also 33% off), with a sharp, colorful AMOLED screen, physical buttons, and top-tier GPS and heart rate tracking. It also tracks heart rate variability (HRV) and resting heart rate. Realistic race time predictions, Training Readiness and Training Status scores, customizable data screens, and daily suggested workouts help runners plan their training.

The Forerunner 265 is built for runners who want more training data than a general fitness or lifestyle watch offers. It’s a step up from the Forerunner 165 thanks to the addition of multi-band GPS and the Training Readiness and Training Status features. If you want a running watch that goes beyond basic features, it's a worthy contender, and even more so at Amazon’s Black Friday sale price.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’re shaken and stirred after this week in film and TV, Insiders. Jesse Whittock with you to recall events as the world was introduced to the latest James Bond.

According to recent reports, “Welcome to the world’s most exclusive club”: And now we know the identity of the next 007. Robert Pattinson is stepping into the well-heeled shoes of James Bond and will star in the next three films from the spy franchise. Pattinson beat out competition from the likes of Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor after emerging as one of the five Deadline revealed a few weeks back would test for the iconic role. The decision was immediately divisive: Many people believe Pattinson has the look and the acting chops to do a great job with Bond, while many others feel he’s probably too well-established already (he is the current Batman!) for a role that has broadly made stars of relative unknowns. Baz Bamigboye’s wonderful column on the casting summed it up, including a quote from a feature film biz source who groaned, “Bond is mysterious. Bond creates the stars. The stars don’t create Bond… For f*ck’s sake!” In the end, Denis Villeneuve went for an actor he knows and trusts – Pattinson will soon be seen in the Canadian director’s Dune: Part Three. The revelation that Amazon boss Jeff Bezos played a large role in the selection didn’t go down well below the line, with one commenter writing, “Pretty awful seeing the fate of James Bond in the hands of a real-life Bond villain.” Since Amazon bought the Broccoli family out of the Bond franchise, there has been industry chatter that the tech and streaming giant would need a bona fide star – someone seriously bankable – to recoup the massive outlay. In R-Patz, they’ve certainly got that: he’s acted in everything from the Twilight movies to Christopher Nolan’s Tenet through to The Batman, and much-loved indie pics such as The Lighthouse and this year’s Primetime, as Dessi Gomez’s gallery item demonstrates. Villeneuve is now designing Bond’s next assignment, but we don’t know when exactly the first Pattinson film is coming. For now, the newest spy on the block should grab a minute to take it all in, say Bond’s of years past. “Welcome to the world’s most exclusive club, but remember to enjoy yourself,” On Her Majesty’s Secret Service star George Lazenby told Pattinson in a sweet video in the hours after the biggest casting news of the year. Related Stories Casting Pierce Brosnan Bonds With Robert Pattinson Over 007 Role News 'Primetime' Cinematographer & Editor On Making Robert Pattinson Look Like A "Superhero" & Breakdown Viral Meme Catchphrase.

Industry observers note that accountability demanded: It’s been a traumatic few weeks in the British entertainment industry. First, Russell Brand was found guilty of sex crimes, followed by revelations about David Walliams’ alleged conduct. Former Doctor Who actor Noel Clarke was also in court this week. He will stand trial next year after pleading not guilty to five sex offence charges. The UK industry is facing a reckoning, and this week a group of actors and other creatives – including Natalie Dormer, Richard Armitage and Susan Wokoma – signed an open letter demanding an end to a “culture of open secrets” in the entertainment industry. The letter called out broadcasters, studios, indies, industry organizations and unions, urging them to review processes, protect whistleblowers and those speaking out, and to “become less offended by your inaction being named than you are by the actions you are being asked to recognize.”.

In a recent development, digging it: Another group of young British writing hopefuls had their moment in the sun this week as the latest Brit List of yet-to-be-produced film and TV screenplays was revealed. Topping the pile was Gemmy Addy’s coming-of-age feature script Dig For Victory and Archie Thomson’s Cornish crime series Petroc, both of which got 25 industry recommendations. We once again partnered with The Brit List to bring you interviews with the writers, with Addy telling us her grandmother’s World War II experiences inspired her story and Thomson attributing his script’s success to influence from England’s West County… and Taylor Sheridan. Read more about The Brit List here.

🌶️ Hot One: Netflix has announced the start of production on Juan Diego Botto‘s domestic violence drama Patricia starring Penélope Cruz, who also produces.

🌶️ Another: Mosquito Coast star Melissa George is leading a BBC and BritBox detective series set around Scotland’s most famous mystery.

🔥 Fiery Third: A second season of breakout Australian drama The Airport Chaplain is coming together, with producer Wooden Horse building a writers’ room.

🤝 A deal, finally: Equity and Pact shook hands on a new deal for British actors, with Max breaking news of a potential agreement hours before it was ratified.

✂️ Cut: The BBC deleted a clip of Russell Brand’s prison message after it was played on the flagship Radio 4 Today show following a “miscommunication.”.

⛺ Fest in Focus: Omar Sy and Joe Russo are among the guests at the revamped Doha Film Festival, as Melanie’s scenesetter noted.

🏏 Howzat!: England cricket legend Ben Stokes has rolled out a production manufacturer.

👨🏻‍⚕️ Doctor, Doctor!: The BBC has drawn up the list of potential producers who will regenerate Doctor Who.

👀 First look: At Minnie Driver in Paramount+’s British heist drama series The Day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iPadOS 27.3 is now in beta and will launch to all users next month, here are three new features it introduces for iPad.

According to recent reports, there’s a fresh setting in iPadOS 27.3 that I instantly turned on and have been loving. It lets you double-tap the top of a window to resize it.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if ‘Windowed Apps’ is enabled there’s now a latest toggle: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom.’.

I’ve been using this gesture all the time in the beta, because it lets me resize my window to fullscreen then revert it to its previous size with ease. It’s an intuitive, convenient way to resize windows for different tasks.

Read more: iPadOS 27.3 adds upcoming iPad setting I instantly turned on.

Visual intelligence was available on iPad already, but iPadOS 27.3 adds a dedicated hub for using the feature: a latest Siri mode in the Camera app.

iOS 27 brought Siri mode to the iPhone’s Camera app, but it was missing from iPad. iPadOS 27.3 corrects that oversight, letting you use your iPad’s built-in Camera app to ask Siri about any object you capture.

Baking visual intelligence into Camera should expose the feature to a lot more iPad users, since before you had to set up a custom control or shortcut for it. And with how much better visual intelligence has gotten thanks to Siri AI, the Siri mode is a valuable addition.

Read more: iOS 27 gives the Camera app on iPhone a brand new mode.

Industry observers note that freeform is gaining a variety of latest features in iPadOS 27.3. They’re available in macOS and iOS too, but out of all Apple platforms, Freeform feels very much built for the iPad.

Industry observers note that which iPadOS 27.3 features are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.

In a recent development, black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but the early Black Friday sales are in full swing. I've been keeping an eye on all the best fitness trackers and smartwatch deals so that you can snag the best possible price from now until the end of Cyber Monday (Nov. 30). Whether you want a full-featured fitness smartwatch or a more recovery-focused tracker, here are the discounts you can find right now, including on brands like Apple, Oura, Garmin, and more.

The Oura Ring 5 is at its lowest ever price: $299 for black and silver, $399 for all other colors. These are the lowest prices ever for these rings, which usually go for $399 and $499, respectively. The Oura Ring 5 is the smallest and most comfortable smart ring I've tried, although it's worth noting it requires a $5.99/month subscription fee.

According to recent reports, for an even cheaper deal, the older Oura Ring 4 is $249—a full $100 off its list price of $349. If you opt for "stealth" (matte black), the price is $279; for gold, it's $286.61, down from $399. While this model has since been replaced by the Oura Ring 5, it's still an accurate and comfortable smart ring—especially if tracking your sleep is your priority.

Whoop may be one of the most expensive smart bands out there, thanks to its subscription-only model. But that price is particularly low right now, since the Peak membership that normally goes for $239 is now $199. Peak is the middle tier, and it's the one I recommend. While you can get Whoop One for $189 in this sale, the $10 you save isn't really worth it given the features you'd be missing. I also wouldn't normally recommend Whoop Life, since its ECG readings and blood pressure estimates aren't really worth the extra $100+. That mentioned, if you do want it, the Life tier is $299 right now instead of $359.

Sources indicate that the latest Luna band is on sale for $119.20, down from a normal price of $149. The Luna band is made by Indian smartwatch company Noise, the same company behind the Luna Ring that I reviewed last year. The ring is no longer available in the U.S., but the band is. It's a Whoop-style screenless fitness tracker, potentially a worthy competitor to the Fitbit Air and other smart bands.

This is the brand-upcoming Apple Watch model, and it's actually worth the upgrade. One of the biggest reasons is that the Series 12's new processor (called, confusingly, the S11 chip) supports some features older Apple Watches can't, and a good rule of thumb is that whenever there's a break in software compatibility, it makes sense to get the newer model. Right now, I'm seeing it for as low as $329, down from the list price of $399. (And if you're stuck deciding between an Apple Watch and a Fitbit, Beth breaks it all down in her comparison of the two watches.).

Sources indicate that the CMF Watch 3 Pro is Nothing's latest smartwatch, and it incorporates AI features powered by ChatGPT; you can at the moment pick it up at a major discount. Originally $99, you can get the CMF Watch 3 Pro for $55. This is the lowest price this smartwatch has been.

If you're looking specifically for a sporty, outdoors watch, Garmin sets the standard. (You could definitely call me something of a Garmin enthusiast.) Here are the best Black Friday deals on Garmin watches that I've seen so far:.

Sources indicate that the 44mm Garmin Instinct 3 is 249.99 (down from $449.99). The 1.2-inch color AMOLED display makes the screen more readable in bright daylight conditions, and battery life is best-in-class—a must for those going off-grid.

The Garmin Fēnix 8 in titanium with a gray band is $749.99 (down from $999.99). While this is last year's model, it's a perfectly solid option if you don't specifically need the titanium case or the latest mapping engine in the latest Fenix 9 Pro.

The Garmin Forerunner 265 is $299.99 (down from $449.99). Although it isn't the latest and greatest anymore, this is still a fan favorite among Garmin owners. It's a step above entry-level options, with dual-band GPS, power meter compatibility, and advanced analytics (like training status).

According to recent reports, halide 3.4 is out today as the latest upgrade to the pro camera app. The update adds several new features, including a larger viewfinder for iPhone Duo and more.

The new Halide patch also lets you use the outer screen on iPhone Duo as a live preview or a fill flash. It brings back a few camera tools from Halide Mark II as well.

According to recent reports, in low light, Halide can use the outer screen as a fill flash. That gives you a softer source of light for portraits, and Halide’s developers recommend turning the screen brightness all the way up before taking the photo.

Sources indicate that halide also now places the histogram along the Duo’s crease. The upgrade revises the Photo Lab interface for editing with the Duo half open as well.

On other iPhones, Halide 3.4 restores the color and luminance histograms and the shutter timer from Mark II.

Halide Mark III released back in May with a redesigned camera and the new Photo Lab editor. Recent updates added RAW-only capture in 3.1 and Aperture Priority for iPhone 18 Pro in 3.2. Halide Mark III version 3.4 is available now on the App Store.

EXCLUSIVE: Watermelon Pictures has acquired North American distribution rights from Global Constellation to coming-of-age drama Ish out of the American Film Market.

The feature directorial debut of British artist and filmmaker Imran Perretta won the Audience Award at the 2025 Venice International Film Festival’s Critics’ Week.

According to recent reports, the film explores friendship, identity and the challenges of adolescence through the experiences of two young boys whose lives are forever changed by a traumatic encounter with police. Related Stories News Susan Sarandon & Aubrey Plaza Drama 'The Accompanist' Gets North American Deal With Watermelon Pictures Documentary Watermelon Pictures Condemns Killing Of 'American Doctor' Surgeon In Gaza Hospital Strike.

Sources indicate that the deal was negotiated by Munir Atalla, Head of Production & Acquisitions at Watermelon Pictures, and Fabien Westerhoff, Managing Director Film of Global Constellation, which represents worldwide sales on behalf of the filmmakers. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that co-written by Perretta and Tony and BAFTA-winning writer Enda Walsh (Hunger), Ish “follows 12-year-old best friends Ish and Maram, whose close bond is shaken following a distressing police stop and search. As the incident’s emotional repercussions unfold, the boys struggle to understand their changing relationship while confronting questions of masculinity, loss and belonging.”.

The film introduces newcomers Farhan Hasnat and Yahya Kitana in the lead roles, alongside Avin Shah, Sudha Bhuchar and BRIT Award-nominated singer-songwriter Joy Crookes, making her feature film acting debut.

In a recent development, pic is produced by BIFA-winning Breakthrough Producer Dhiraj Mahey of Primal Pictures (The Ghoul) and Bennett McGhee of Home Team (Mogul Mowgli), in association with Mike Goodridge of Good Chaos (Triangle of Sadness). The film was developed and financed by BBC Film and the BFI, alongside additional financing from Calculus Media and Dorian Grinspan’s Out of Order. Eric Kuhn (Grand Theft Hamlet) serves as executive producer.

Recent findings suggest that the film features black-and-white cinematography by Jermaine Canute Edwards (My Father’s Shadow), editing by Adam Biskupski (Mogul Mowgli), and sound design by Jens Rosenlund Petersen and Academy Award and BAFTA winner Nina Hartstone (Bohemian Rhapsody). Perretta also composed the film’s original score.

It has been revealed that “Ish is a beautifully realized and deeply affecting film that captures the complexities of growing up with remarkable honesty and sensitivity,” mentioned Munir Atalla, Head of Production & Acquisitions at Watermelon Pictures. “Imran Perretta brings an extraordinary visual perspective to a story that feels both intimate and universal, exploring friendship, identity and the lasting impact of injustice. We are proud to champion his feature debut and introduce this powerful film to North American audiences.”.

Faben Westerhoff, MD Film, Global Constellation, added: “Imran’s transition into feature filmmaking is a masterclass in visual storytelling and emotional honesty. We are delighted to partner with Watermelon on this release. They are the ideal North American distributor for Ish, fearless champions of distinctive, culturally resonant cinema that strikes a deep chord with contemporary audiences.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27 gave AirPods Pro a variety of upcoming features, but there’s another addition that’s easy to miss: a convenient new setting in Control Center for Adaptive Audio.

Several AirPods models offer excellent Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes—especially AirPods Pro 3 (now only $179).

It has been revealed that but Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a newly introduced setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

It has been revealed that while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

New in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

Industry observers note that you can also move the fresh slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Sources indicate that do you ever use Adaptive Audio, and if so, have you adjusted it at all? Let us know in the comments.

The controversy stems from Alle Elsker Rasmus, a series that introduced on October 26, in which comedian Rasmus Wallbridge was deceived into believing his dream comedy-horror film project was being produced. Well over 100 people were involved with the production, many of whom were in on the prank. Secret cameras filmed Wallbridge as he remained unaware of the true nature of the situation.

What resulted was a Truman Show-style reality series, and Alle Elsker Rasmus met with immediate and severe backlash from the public and the Danish government. It was quickly taken off air and TV2 issued an apology to Wallbridge.

The comedian himself has been relatively relaxed about the prank, which was led by his creative partner, Martin Johannes Larsen, host of Denmark’s civilian version of The Traitors. Wallbridge was informed of the show’s true nature before it went out and had to power to block its broadcast, according to the network.

According to recent reports, today, TV2 issued a long statement that noted an investigation into Alle Elsker Rasmus was ongoing, having begun earlier this month. The review will “thoroughly examine the process surrounding the creation and publication of the series, and – where relevant – to formulate recommendations for adjusting TV 2’s ethical guidelines,” the broadcaster noted.

In a recent development, drive Studios, known for making Netflix series Behind Every Man and Prime Video’s Girls of Copenhagen, produced the show, and its CEO Kasper Fredshavn has previously issued an apology to Wallbridge. He admitted “the format went too far,” but is not commenting further until the end of the review, with which Drive is cooperating.

Sources indicate that results of the review will be presented to the board “within a few weeks,” the broadcaster said today. “Regardless of the investigation’s outcome, the overall assessment is already that new leadership is required to spearhead the extensive work of following up on the investigation, rebuilding trust, and overseeing future programming activities.”.

The broadcaster mentioned it was “clear that trust in TV2’s programming has been challenged” and that it will “face a process of restoration.” Its statement added that criticism over the show was “justified” and added: “We must always insist that quality content serves the public, shows consideration for the individuals involved, is rooted in a shared understanding of ethics, and remains relevant to the Danish people.”.

TV2 paid tribute to Pors as an “outstanding journalist” and a “skilled, respected” media executive, whose work had established the broadcaster as “the leading news broadcaster in Denmark,” and called Thirstrup “a passionate advocate for public service broadcasting,” and a “skilled and empathetic leader.”.

Pors took to social media to address her exit. “After nearly an entire professional life – serving in roles ranging from US correspondent, editor-in-chief, and News Director to, most recently, Content Director at TV 2 – it is now time to say goodbye,” she wrote.

“Following the series Alle elsker Rasmus, TV2 will install upcoming leadership to rebuild trust in the broadcaster’s programming and its relationships with external producers. That’s just how it is. For now, I am stepping away and have no further comments, but I look forward to new challenges, conversations, and whatever else the future may hold.”.

I tested the Hyundai Ioniq 9 again for the second time this year — don't let its polarizing design fool you

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks.
  • In a recent development, that’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there.
  • According to recent reports, but after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks. In fact, I said in my 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 review that the design is an “odd mashup featuring a curvy front bumper with an even stranger-looking arched rear.” It’s one of the last SUVs I’d expect to win any beauty awards.

In a recent development, that’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there. I’ve spent more time testing 3-row SUVs than any other vehicle type this year, with models like the Kia Telluride, Volvo XC90, Volkswagen Atlas, and Lucid Gravity getting my seal of approval.

According to recent reports, but after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake. Here’s what I realized.

Best long distance driving efficiency.

Best short distance driving efficiency.

According to recent reports, as with most vehicles, fuel economy and efficiency tend to dwindle over time — which is why I’m shocked that the Ioniq 9 is an exception. I was already impressed by the 3 mi/kWh average I got when I drove it last year, yet my second run delivered even better results.

Across 130.5 miles of mixed driving, my second go-around with the Ioniq 9 yielded an impressive 3.3 mi/kWh. What surprised me even more was the substantial improvement in city driving, where I recorded a peak tally of 4.5 mi/kWh — up from my previous best of 3.8 mi/kWh.

It has been revealed that considering it’s marketed as a three-row family hauler, it’s remarkable that the Ioniq 9 can post numbers like this. That extra efficiency is critical, too: while this trim carries an EPA-estimated range of 311 miles, averaging 3.3 mi/kWh puts its real-world range closer to 363 miles.

I’ll admit I was harsh on the Hyundai Ioniq 9’s styling the first time around. While it certainly takes cues from the subcompact Hyundai Kona, I argued that it was an odd mashup that was confused about what aesthetic it was trying to go after.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

After spending another week with it, though, its unconventional look slowly grew on me — even if that appreciation is mostly isolated to the front of the EV. That’s due to Hyundai’s signature Parametric Pixel LED light bar, which stretches across the nose like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Those individual blocks give it a retro look that becomes even more dazzling from dusk into the night. In a sea of generic crossovers, this one certainly commands road presence.

According to recent reports, that remarked, I still haven’t come to terms with the back half of this electric SUV. That tapered, upright rear end remains the hardest pill to swallow, giving it the look of a boat tail. Despite this, I now appreciate that the shape is doing the heavy lifting to make it aerodynamic — and subsequently boosting its efficiency.

It has been revealed that whether I’m making a quick stop at the local grocery store or on my 30+ mile commute to work, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 doesn’t skimp on the comforts. Step inside, and it’s clear Hyundai prioritized first-class comfort for the people riding up front and in the middle.

Sources indicate that for example, the plush H-Tex seats strike a great balance of softness and support — which, for the driver, includes extra pampering courtesy of Hyundai’s Ergo Motion seat. When activated, it slowly adjusts the firmness of the cushion, sort of like getting a mini massage while driving, all to deter fatigue on longer hauls.

Still, the real VIP treatment belongs to the second-row captain’s chairs. With both heating and ventilation, plus power-reclining backrests and extendable footrests, they turn the middle row into a rolling lounge. However, the third row leaves more to be desired. Although I still appreciate having the extra seating capacity in a pinch, the legroom back there is practically nonexistent for adults — so I’d much rather keep that rear bench folded flat to make way for more trunk space.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design comes loaded with just about every luxury and tech perk anyone could ask for — and rightfully so.

​I still absolutely love Hyundai's adaptive cruise control, which makes long drives bearable and includes a dedicated lane-centering button on the steering wheel that also happens to work on local roads. Adding to that is a crisp Head-Up Display that projects my speed and navigation right onto the windshield.

​Changing lanes is effortless thanks to the Blind-Spot View Monitor (which streams a live camera feed straight into the digital gauge cluster) and a digital rearview mirror that offers a wider field of view than a conventional glass mirror.

​Back-seat passengers get plenty of love, too, with built-in rear side-window sunshades, a massive panoramic sunroof, and dazzling customizable ambient lighting that sets an upscale mood after dark.

​There’s also practical utility in the form of a handy 120V outlet accessible right in the trunk, letting me power laptops, tailgating gear, or small appliances straight off the SUV’s battery.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design is easily one of the most expensive vehicles in Hyundai’s entire lineup — and that price tag has long made me a skeptic.

​Yet spending a second week behind the wheel proved that judging it at face value is a mistake. Between its even better real-world efficiency, spacious cabin suited for families, and a laundry list of thoughtful luxury features, the Ioniq 9 delivers where it counts most: a family hauler that's rich in utility and backed by an efficient drive.

The Making of Oxygene

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Jeanmicheljarre

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in late 1976, an album was released which re-wrote the rulebook of synthesizers and electronic music and captured the hearts and imagination of the entire world.
  • Uniquely, the album consisted of just six tracks, numbered Oxygène Parts 1 through 6, and was entirely instrumental with no acoustic instruments whatsoever, which was unheard of in 1976.
  • Jean Michel Jarre tells the story of the making of his ground-breaking album in his own words.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in late 1976, an album was released which re-wrote the rulebook of synthesizers and electronic music and captured the hearts and imagination of the entire world. Composed by the then unknown 28-year-old French artist Jean-Michel Jarre, the album Oxygène broke out of France to become a top 10 album in seven different countries, spending a remarkable 24 weeks in the UK album charts and selling now close to 20 million copies worldwide.

Uniquely, the album consisted of just six tracks, numbered Oxygène Parts 1 through 6, and was entirely instrumental with no acoustic instruments whatsoever, which was unheard of in 1976.

Jean Michel Jarre tells the story of the making of his ground-breaking album in his own words.

"Around 1969, I felt that the world of classical music, the world of rock and other forms of music were a bit narrow and living in their own worlds. I had the feeling it was the right time to explore other fields to perhaps see if a combination of different styles were possible.

“The main difference with electronic music is that you create music in terms of sound, not just notes. It’s something else entirely. When I was a teenager, I always liked processing my guitar or organ or whatever, playing the tape backwards and changing the speed. Then the drummer in my band stated, ‘You should meet with these crazy guys at Groupe De Recherches Musicales [GRM] in Paris who are working in French public radio. They’re doing the same kinds of things as you, and they have labs.’.

“When I first went there, I was immediately seduced by what they were doing. Electronic music owes a lot to public radio stations - the BBC Radiophonic Workshop, the German lab where Stockhausen was working and, of course, the one in Paris.

"Pierre Schaeffer was one of the most brilliant guys of the century in terms of what he brought to the music world. He created the notion of Musique concrète and influenced me a lot in this direction. Saying that, I felt that contemporary music had got a very elitist attitude - a bit too intellectual vis-à-vis the music and it created barriers between the audience and yourself. I wanted to be much more open to the audience.

In a recent development, "I stayed with Pierre Schaeffer [and Pierre Henry] for three years and I also went to Cologne to work with Stockhausen. He was totally crazy, but a real genius. He considered himself to be made of sound, biologically, so he had a kind of surrealistic approach. Crazy, but realistic at the same time. It was very interesting.

"When I left GRM and through to 1976, I did production work for some rock artists, earning enough to set up a studio in my kitchen. I didn’t have much equipment, though, just a few guitar pedals and my first synthesizer, the VCS3, which looked like a telephone exchange. I realised that using a Revox tape machine to delay the sound that came out of one loudspeaker created a huge sense of space.

Sources indicate that “The British-made VCS3 from EMS [Electronic Music Studios, based in London] was created by a genius called Peter Zinovieff. It was a kind of poor European version of the Moog. In those days Europe was not as rich as the States, so the sound was drier. In a sense, it was a kind of punk synthesizer - there was something very harsh and rough about it. I loved it; I still take one on stage with me today.

“At the time, I was obsessed with this idea of creating a bridge between experimentation and pop melody. I liked this kind of challenge, playing around with sound design and integrating melodies. Oxygène was a new start for music with analogue synthesizers".

The album was recorded on a Scully recorder with just eight tracks, and all through a home-made mixer. On top of the VCS3, Jarre had managed to add some other classic equipment including EMS Synthi AKS and ARP 2600 synths, an Eminent String Ensemble, an RMI Harmonic Synthesizer, and Farfisa organ, while an RMI Keyboard Computer was used for some sequencing.

Sources indicate that jarre continues, “I really did it in a kind of home way using what, I think, was one of the first home studios. I had just three or four synthesizers and was using a Scully eight–track and a mixture of Ampex 256 and 3M tape. The whole album was done on just one eight–track and you can hear that in the piece — it’s quite minimalist and I think that contributes to its timelessness.

Sources indicate that “Nothing is repeated the same way. Each sound, even if appears to be the same, has a slightly different attack and release, and, as the sequences are being made by hand, by definition they are not the same. Even the sounds of the drum machines were filtered in a very subtle way to give life inside the patterns.

It has been revealed that ”Michel Geiss was a maintenance technician, at a famous French record organization at that time called Barclay and I met him because he was very interested in electronic instruments. He visited my home and we started to experiment. He was teaching me to use the first semi-modular synths I could put my hands on. And then step by step we worked together, Michel mainly as a kind of sound engineer for me.

“For Oxygene, he was working at his record company as a maintenance guy during the day, and he was coming to work with me at night. In those days I probably had the first home studio in France, when the serious music was done in serious recording studios with a window where God was the sound engineer behind the window, and we were just on the other side as musicians. For electronic music you need to match the mixing area with the main studio to record your own sounds.

“So, I had this home studio in a kitchen in the flat I had in Paris, and Michel joined me, using one of the first eight-track tape recorders to record my music. I only had two tapes. So, I had no choice if I was not happy with something to erase what I'd done the previous day, and this is the reason why I have no archive of material from Oxygène. It's such a shame.

Industry observers note that “And that is also the reason why if you take the master tape of Oxygène, it is made up of two different tapes. Right in the middle of part one of Oxygène, I had one piece I really liked, where suddenly in the first part you have this kind of brassy, quite epic brassy moment. This is coming from another tape that I recorded another time.

Sources indicate that “I thought to myself that it's really matching very well. So, I did a very strong edit, quite dramatic edit, by cutting the two tapes together, even the colours are different. One is pink, one is black. It's totally crazy. And whilst you can't hear the edit, it's quite challenging to cut an eight-track tape like this.

“With so little to work with, I had to be creative. My old Mellotron only had a few working keys, but I still managed to write Oxygene Part II on it. My primitive drum machine - a Korg Mini Pops was the sort of thing people played in pubs, but by using Sellotape I could make it play two preset rhythms at the same time, creating cool beats. Oxygène Part IV, which became iconic, was a mixture of [presets] Slow Rock and Rock, while Part VI combined Rumba and Bossa Nova.

According to recent reports, “But when I finished the album, because Oxygène consisted of entirely instrumental music, none of the record companies thought it would work. The only people who took the risk were a small French company called Dreyfus Music. Even after it had become a hit in France, people said it couldn't possibly be a success anywhere else. Then eventually, after it got to the top of the charts in Britain and all over Europe, the critics explained that it was successful because of its originality and because of its use of melody. It's easy to be wise after the event!

“I made the first album back in the days of vinyl, when we were always thinking about sides one and two. The other characteristic of Oxygène is that it has sunny melodies but it’s also quite dark, like the cover artwork.”.

It has been revealed that studio engineer and would-be long-time collaborator Michel Geiss, has fond memories of his first encounter with Jean Michel Jarre, recalling, "Oxygene marked the beginning of my collaboration with Jean-Michel. At the time, I was working during the day at a large studio complex in Paris called Studios Barclay. I was employed there as a technician. The recording studios were located on the upper floors, while I worked in the workshop downstairs. My body was downstairs, but my mind was upstairs! I felt strongly attracted to the world of music engineering, although I wasn't particularly interested in the equipment I had been assigned to work with.

"In fact, I found the right balance when I began working with Jean-Michel at his own studio around the same time. Every day, once my working day at Barclay had finished, I would join Jean-Michel in his studio, at his request, to work on his album. We would continue until I had to catch the last train home. I remember him calling me every afternoon to ask if I could come over.

In a recent development, "This was my first real opportunity to work in a studio as a sound and music collaborator, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. Jean-Michel would also occasionally ask for my musical opinion on various matters. I programmed some specific sounds on the ARP 2600, including the main theme sound in Oxygene IV and the sound of the waves in Part VI.

Sources indicate that "It was a close working relationship, and I felt that I had finally found my rightful place. It suited me much better than simply being an electronics specialist, which was my background before I met him.

"My main role during the recording of Oxygene was to record Jean-Michel while he played his instruments, as he needed someone to handle the recording process.

It has been revealed that "At the time, he was also keen to expand his relatively limited collection of instruments in order to explore fresh sounds. I suggested that we take a look at the RMI keyboards, which were sold in France by Piano Center in Montreuil. Jean-Michel immediately agreed, saying, 'OK, let's go!'.

"When we arrived at the music shop, Jean-Michel discovered the two instruments I had suggested: the RMI Harmonic Synthesizer and the RMI Keyboard Computer. The latter used punched cardboard cards to store its sound information. The Harmonic Synthesizer had a truly distinctive sound and featured an arpeggiator. It would later prove to be a key instrument on the album, particularly on Oxygene IV.".

The album’s iconic artwork came about when Jarre was visiting Marquet Gallery in Paris and a piece caught his eye that he was instantly drawn to. A painting of a skull hidden within the Earth. The painting was created by young artist Michel Granger, titled Oxygène. By chance, Granger happened to be in the gallery at the same time and the pair spoke and Jean-Michel bought the painting to use as the album cover and adopted its title.

Industry observers note that michel Granger recalls, “I was having my first major show in Paris. On display was a 30x40cm watercolour called Oxygène and Jean-Michel bought it, telling me he’d love to use it as an album cover. Oxygène was part of a series about the damage being done to our planet. It was quite a violent image for a record sleeve.

Recent findings suggest that “The only change I made was to the background, making it square to fit the album shape. Jean-Michel and I chose the typography and that was that. We were both similar ages and he was very passionate about music and painting. We would have long conversations in the evenings, always at the same pizzeria, then he went home to compose all night.”.

Jean Michel Jarre commented on the artwork,"What I like about this picture is that it isn’t necessarily pessimistic. It rather poses the question: where are we going?”.

With its iconic title and cover set, and after the album was mixed at Studio Gang by Jean-Pierre Janiaud, an accomplished engineer, Jarre took the album to Francis Dreyfus, owner of the Disques Motors record label, who he had worked for during his songwriting days with Christophe. Dreyfus loved the album and was convinced it could be a success.

Industry observers note that dreyfus pressed 50,000 copies on his own label to sell in France and released the album in December 1976. Uniquely and a brainwave of Dreyfus and Jarre, they offered the album to nationwide hi-fi shops, given the album's innovative use of stereo. The idea being that high-end hi-fi buyers would buy a copy of the album to go with their hardware purchase. By April 1977, sales in France had reached 70,000 copies despite very little promotion. Legend has it that some people returned the LP believing the iconic white noise was a manufacturing defect.

Sources indicate that finding an international label to distribute was harder. Initially no record manufacturer was interested in the album, citing no singer, no guitars, no drummer, no proper track titles, no obvious singles, and to round it off, it was French.

Everything changed when Fred Haayen, the newly introduced head of Polydor Records in London discovered the record in a French record store and signed it to the label. He was instrumental in persuading BBC Radio 1 to play the album in full the week of release. The only other album to ever receive such an honour was Pink Floyd's Dark Side of the Moon.

The album was mostly slated by the UK's mainstream music press, with the NME calling it “another interminable sonic cruise and infuriatingly derivative.” but the public loved the album and on August 23rd 1977, Oxygène entered the UK album charts at number 19, climbing and remaining in the top 10 for the next 11 weeks. After moving to the United States to lead Polydor USA, Haayen also spearheaded the launch of the album in the US, to achieve official platinum status.

According to recent reports, we’ll let Jarre conclude the story, “It’s now sold something like 18 million copies and, no matter what I do, I am defined by Oxygène. But that’s OK. It’s funny. At first, the album was played in hi-fi shops as an example of 'state-of-the-art sound'. I didn’t tell them I made it in my kitchen.

Recent findings suggest that “When you’ve been lucky enough to have some kind of success with your first project, it will always be part of your DNA, no matter what you do afterwards. It’s like the first movie for Tarantino or Kubrick. For me, it’s the same with Oxygène. I love many other things that I’ve done and I’m very proud of them all, but Oxygène is something unique.”.

Google is upgrading the Gemini app on Mac with computer use capabilities that can work across local desktop applications and the web.

The existing Task (previously Gemini Spark) functionality in the Mac app could just access local files in conjunction with Connected Apps, like @Gmail or @Google Calendar.

Computer use lets Gemini for Mac click and type on your behalf to accomplish multi-step tasks in local desktop apps and the web, like navigating menus and filling out forms.

Gemini works in an “isolated background window with a live preview right in your chat,” while your main screen and cursor remain free to use. On the safety front, you can stop Gemini at any time with one click, while you choose what apps Gemini uses. Google will pause for logins and payments, with confirmation needed for sensitive actions.

Many everyday tasks span desktop apps and websites that don’t connect to each other. Computer use handles the tedious steps in the background so you can save time without giving up your screen or cursor.

To use, add @Computer use to your prompt. In Customize > Connectors, you’ll see upcoming “Desktop” apps like Blender and Autodesk Fusion join the existing Git and Obsidian integrations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Giant K-pop show the MAMA Awards 2026 is taking place in Osaka, Japan, this weekend,a and the first winners have been crowed.

BTS won the coveted Artist of the Year category for the eighth time, and Enhypen won three: Fans’ Choice of the Year, Favorite M-Countdown Stage and Fan’s Choice Top 10 – Male. Ive won Best Female Group.

The music event, which broadcasts in Korea on Mnet, brings together Korean music performers from across generations over two nights.

When Life Gives You Tangerines actor Park Bo-gum, who has become the first MAMA Awards ambassador, hosted night one at the Kyocera Dome this evening, marking his eighth time hosting times since 2017. Related Stories News First-Ever 'Saturday Night Live' International Spin-Off Lands In Korea News Disney+ & Netflix Hoover Up Non-English Acquisitions As Fervor For Japanese & Korean Content Continues - Ampere.

This year’s awards saw boy band Enhypen turn Dune: Part Three, which opens in December, into a K-pop performance. The MAMA Awards will also see K-pop veterans BIGBANG perform alongside Dooly the Little Dinosaur, one of Korea’s most beloved animated characters, who was created by cartoonist Kim Soo-jung in 1983. Watch on Deadline.

The awards have benefitted from the explosion in interest in Korean culture. Having started as domestic awards ceremony in 1999, MAMA became the first K-pop ceremony to be held overseas, and in 2024 it also took place in the U.S. for the first time. “MAMA Awards has grown alongside K-POP’s global growth, we believe these efforts have created more ways for artists and fans around the world to connect,” stated Yoon Shin Hye, who is head of CJ ENM-owned Mnet.

“Over the past 27 years, MAMA Awards has expanded its stages to places it had never been, connected artists and fans in ways never seen before, and been the first to show K-pop’s upcoming possibilities,” added Harry H.K. Shin, Head of Music Entertainment at CJ ENM in a statement. “All of that was possible with our one firm belief: ‘Music Makes One.’.

“This year, we want to once again deliver an experience where people connect through music, beyond the boundaries of time and space, generation and region.”.

Industry observers note that the awards come at an notable juncture for K-pop music. The global glare has put K-pop under the microscope and a recent Latest York Times article about restrictions within artist contracts caused major debate, prompting the K-pop music association to hit back and defend the industry.

The South Korean government earlier this week noted it would undertake a survey to assess how underage performers were treated. Asked about the health of K-pop, Yoon said the industry relied on finding latest successes, and, “For that to happen, the creativity of everyone who makes music, not just the artists but also the songwriters, producers, choreographers, directors and creators, needs to be respected.”.

Yoon was keen the point to the unifying nature of the awards for fans. “At MAMA Awards, they can discover the same songs, share what they like and connect through music. What we want to show through this year’s theme, ‘a music interstellar,’ is fans from different generations and different parts of the world coming together and discovering new moments.”.

Here’s an interview with Yoon conducted before to night’s ceremony.

DEADLINE: What scale of investment does the event take to organise?

Yoon Shin Hye: MAMA Awards is much more than an awards ceremony. It’s a major global project that brings together CJ ENM’s music, broadcasting and global network, along with its production capabilities. I can’t disclose specific figures, but it takes experts across many fields and a lot of infrastructure. Everything from creative planning, stage production and direction to cutting-edge technology, global live broadcasting and on-site operations goes into bringing each artist’s performance to life.

And because MAMA Awards has to reflect each year’s K-pop’s trends and where the industry is heading, we start preparing at the very beginning of the year. Throughout the year, we meet fans through M Countdown, our Mnet weekly K-POP chart show, and KCON, our K-Pop festival in places like Japan and the U.S. All of that leads up to MAMA AWARDS, where global fandoms come together as one. So really, MAMA is the result of a year-long journey.

DEADLINE: What are you trying to show the world with this event?

YSH: We truly believe music can bring people together, regardless of language, nationality, culture or generation. MAMA Awards is where artists and fans from all over the world get to experience that together. Mnet, which hosts the awards, started as a music channel in 1995 and turned 30 last year. Over those three decades, we’ve grown up alongside generations of K-pop, introducing artists’ music and performances and bringing them closer to fans worldwide. MAMA Awards has been part of that journey, growing with K-Pop and becoming a global stage where artists meet fans around the world.

DEADLINE: What are the highlights of the event and can you hint at any surprises?

YSH: This year, I’d say the thing to look out for is performances and collaborations that cross generations, genres and cultures. First, you’ll see different generations of K-Pop on one stage. There’s Panic, the legendary Korean duo celebrating 31 years since their debut in 1995, and BIGBANG marking their 20th anniversary. And alongside them, artists who debuted at every point from the early 2000s right up to 2026.

We’ve also got some exciting projects where K-pop meets global entertainment: Enhypehm teaming up with Dune: Part Three for MAMA Awards’ signature Cinematic Stage, which brings the film’s world into a K-pop performance. And BIGBANG is pairing up with Dooly the Little Dinosaur, a much-loved Korean animated character, for a collaboration no one will see coming.

Sources indicate that DEADLINE: K-pop stars and the management companies behind them have been in the light for both good and bad reasons recently. What is your read on the health of the industry right now?

Recent findings suggest that YSH: For K-pop to grow beyond its current global success into a truly sustainable industry, I think it can’t rely only on a handful of big artists or genres that have already proven successful. It needs to be an industry where fresh successes keep emerging, driven by diverse musical experiments and genres, artists with their own distinct identities, and companies of all sizes willing to take on new challenges.

According to recent reports, for that to happen, the creativity of everyone who makes music, not just the artists but also the songwriters, producers, choreographers, directors and creators, needs to be respected. That respect is something we try to reflect in how we put the MAMA Awards together. The MAMA AWARDS also continues to work on bringing fans and artists closer together. Fans and artists are the most vital driving force behind K-POP, so I think it’s important to build a healthy relationship where they have a positive influence on each other, and where fans can freely enjoy and take part in it.

DEADLINE: Can you talk about the why K-pop stars often have ambitions to become film or TV stars?

Recent findings suggest that YSH: I think it’s a very natural progression. K-pop artists are true all-rounders. They sing, dance and perform. Their experience of expressing their individuality and emotions through music and performance, and connecting with fans around the world, can be a strong foundation for taking on creative fields.

Recent findings suggest that these days, the lines between music, film, TV and fashion are really blurring, so I see it as a positive thing that artists are expressing their talent in more ways. Of course, acting requires its own skill and dedication, but these new challenges can help artists grow and find new ways to express themselves. And as K-pop, film, TV and other K-content become more connected, there are more chances to reach new global audiences. I’m looking forward to seeing K-POP artists build on their music and explore their potential in many different fields.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The changing of the clocks has taken its toll on my sleep this Fall. After long evenings bathed in artificial light, I've been feeling more wired than tired at bedtime. But thanks to one surprising gadget, lately I've been more consistent with my bedtime – and that's a good thing as studies link sleep consistency with better life expectancy.

In a recent development, now that I’m prioritising a consistent sleep routine, I’m also waking up less through the night. So what is this surprising gadget? A red light face mask. Were you expecting something different? Mask aside, red light is stated to accentuate the production of sleep hormones.

However, sceptical that I’ve been lulling myself to sleep with nothing more than a placebo effect, I called on double-boarded sleep medicine specialist Dr. Chris Winter to ask whether the science around red lights sleep benefits checks out. Here's what he said...

Due to my job, I have a collection of gadgets to reach for when it comes to bedtime – the Ozlo Sleepbuds, Hatch Sleep Clock and the Oura Ring 5 included.

But one that's really surprised me lately is the Bob and Brad PhysioFace Light Therapy Mask, available for $169.99 (was $199.99) at Amazon.

I've been using the mask, chiefly marketed for skincare purposes, as part of my bedtime routine and it's helped me put down my phone and get to sleep on time.

As much as I love my Hatch clock, I don't love that I have to use my phone to alter settings. That's the beauty of this red light mask – it’s independent from my phone (there's no app to download) with control buttons attached to the device itself.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

That means I am actually making my bedroom a phone-free space and instead focusing on winding down for a great night's sleep.

Recent findings suggest that it's hard to quantify exactly how well the red light mask is improving my sleep quality. But one thing is for sure: by the time I remove the mask, I feel sleepy and it never takes me long to dose off into a deep sleep.

According to my Garmin sleep timeline, I've reached deep sleep within half hour of dropping off, and continue to cycle through healthy sleep stages.

But what does Dr. Winter think? "It’s possible that taking a quiet break for your skincare routine is helping you unwind, particularly if it replaces scrolling or other stimulating activities.

"But feeling that you’re sleeping better doesn’t tell us whether the benefit is coming from the light itself, the routine, or something else.

"I would view it as a potentially relaxing part of your routine — not a proven sleep treatment," the board-certified neurologist cautions.

Recent findings suggest that white and blue light from screens is bad news for sleep. But as the nights draw in, a lot of our evenings are powered by these types of light. This winter, I’ve been making a conscious effort to swap my overhead light for the sundown setting on my Hatch Sleep Clock. I've also been swapping doomscrolling with reading time while wearing my red light mask.

In a recent development, 20 minutes prior to bedtime – after writing my do-to list for the following day and shutting off my phone for the night – I pop the mask on in bed and start reading a book. The 10-minute timer on the mask ensures I read for at least 10 minutes before drifting off.

It has been revealed that the mask has three light modes with different colored lights. I've been using the BOOST mode that combines red light and near-infrared light. As well as supposedly boosting skin health, red light is associated with relaxation and there is some science associating it with improved sleep quality.

Although evidence is limited, research by Chinese scientists published in the National Library of Medicine, suggests red light influences melatonin secretion, improving sleep initiation.

In a recent development, dr. Winter also referred to a 2026 review of five randomized trials that found a modest improvement in self-reported sleep quality when red light was introduced. "But the authors emphasized that the evidence was limited and imprecise," he notes.

Additionally, red light face masks, like my Bob and Brad model, are built to increase collagen production. They do this by penetrating the skin with red light, which stimulates the cells responsible for collagen synthesis. Besides improving skin elasticity, collagen can also improve sleep. A 2024 study concluded that increasing collagen at bedtime reduces sleep fragmentation.

Placebo or not, the mask has helped me prioritise a consistent bedtime routine over the past two weeks, and sleep better than I was immediately after the clock change.

I’ve been writing about sleep for over two years, and one thing I’ve learnt is that your sleep routine must be personal. A gadget or habit that works for someone else may not work for you.

If you’re struggling to sleep, you may need to try a few different methods or technologies before you hit on one that clicks. But one piece of advice sleep experts all agree on is that you need a relaxing prelude to sleep if you want to clock quality ZZZs.

A nighttime routine involves practising the same sequence of activities in the run up to your bedtime, helping prepare both your brain and body for sleep. In time, and with consistency, your body clock will come to recognise this routine as a signal to sleep, helping you drift off easily.

Industry observers note that dr. Winter explains: "A bedtime routine creates a predictable opportunity to step away from work, screens and other stimulating activities, rather than expecting your brain to switch off the moment your head hits the pillow. Pairing that wind-down period with a consistent sleep schedule and lower lighting helps support your body’s sleep-wake rhythm.".

This routine should be "simple, enjoyable and easy to repeat" and can include activity you find relaxing, be that a dark shower, mediation, reading, stretching or simply listening to calm music.

"You don’t need an elaborate checklist or expensive equipment—the goal is to wind down, not give yourself another assignment," advises the host of the Sleep Unplugged podcast.

"Think of the routine as making room for sleep, not forcing it to happen.".

#4425. Industry News: Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (825 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (825 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, stated last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Recent findings suggest that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.
