In a recent development, bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of people. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that new job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the firm has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced prepares to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give consumers more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Sources indicate that over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted fresh job listings that offer a closer look at its intends to develop autonomous AI agents:.

Industry observers note that in one, Apple stated it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

Industry observers note that “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “initiative and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Today’s report on the latest job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring owners to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the tech giant could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how swiftly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally rolled out its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

Latest Update: Scout Motors Is Using AI Earpieces to Train Factory Workers

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, “AI training” usually refers to instilling artificial intelligence with human knowledge.
  • CEO Scott Keogh spoke with CNET during a reporters roundtable at Scout’s still-under-construction factory in Blythewood, South Carolina.
  • Recent findings suggest that keogh described the approach as starting from the work itself.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “AI training” usually refers to instilling artificial intelligence with human knowledge. Scout Motors indicates it’s been doing the opposite: using AI tools to help hire, onboard and train factory workers, including an AI assistant in an earpiece that guides trainees through tasks as they perform them.

CEO Scott Keogh spoke with CNET during a reporters roundtable at Scout’s still-under-construction factory in Blythewood, South Carolina. Keogh noted that rather than “sitting new hires down with an instructional binder and a test,” workers are getting AI-driven, hands-on experience early in a push to make the training more efficient and effective. Meanwhile, the automaker can collect and feed training data back into the system to fine-tune its hiring, training and placement processes.

Recent findings suggest that keogh described the approach as starting from the work itself. Manufacturing, he said, can be broken down into a handful of fundamental tasks, and the AI system is built to teach each one. He offered parts picking as the simplest example: A worker walks to 12 boxes, pulls 12 parts, confirms they’re in the right sequence and checks them for defects. The AI in the earpiece can guide the worker through that sequence, providing real-time, adaptable instructions.

In a recent development, “We can train that within minutes,” Keogh remarked. “A worker repeats the cycle about 15 times, getting faster and better each pass, and then moves down the task line to the next skill.”.

To my ears, that doesn’t sound like the sort of task you’d need an AI system to help with and, to some extent, Scout’s executives agreed.

It has been revealed that however, the automaker’s representatives argued that the new method is far more productive than traditional classroom training — with increasing benefits as the trained tasks and concepts become more complex. Keogh also linked the speed at which the manufacturer has seen its newest factory hires become productive with how quickly Scout can ramp up the factory itself.

It has been revealed that scout execs say AI also plays a role in the hiring and onboarding before training begins. Todd Johnson, vice president of manufacturing, remarked the team feeds newly introduced hires’ backgrounds into an AI system, which suggests where each person might fit best: A former forklift driver might be steered toward logistics, someone with no final assembly experience might do better in the body shop and a person with paint shop experience could be placed as a painter.

According to recent reports, again, that sounded a lot like common sense to me. Isn’t that how people were hired before AI? According to Scout Motors’ leadership, the algorithm can potentially identify less obvious connections between skills and tasks that a human might miss, expanding access to jobs for applicants who may not have received traditional manufacturing training, which is key because Scout’s upcoming plant is located in an area that doesn’t have a large pool of local dyed-in-the-wool traditional automotive workers.

To fill the over 4,000 roles that factory will need to reach full speed ahead by 2028, the automaker claims it’s hiring from a national pool of applicants. However, executives told me that using AI to consider nontraditional factory workers — citing one hire who worked at the DMV — will allow Scout to identify and place more local applicants and bring fresh ideas to the factory floor.

In a recent development, ryan Decker, vice president of strategy and brand, called Scout’s AI-forward approach to placement and training “a passion project for the company.” Decker told CNET that Scout’s training AI can tailor instruction to each person rather than delivering the same material to a room of 10 people over 10 days. People learn differently, he mentioned, with different language skills and levels of technical depth.

According to recent reports, decker also remarked the system is bidirectional. The AI can learn from how each group responds to the training and use that information to modify instruction for the next cohort. Decker thinks that each subsequent batch of workers will be “1% better,” and that after 1,000 repetitions, he expects the AI to be “dialed in and know how to provide information to the people in the most productive way possible.”.

Scout notes it’s also exploring vision-based AI training, in which the trainee is guided via augmented reality glasses, as the next evolution of the technology. The automaker is also looking to eventually expand the tech for do-it-yourself use by owners at home. I imagine a future where owners can use an Apple Vision Pro or similar device — which would be a pricey investment — to guide themselves through installing a roof rack or performing routine maintenance.

In practice, the next step, according to Scout’s execs, is to scale its AI learning tools beyond the training room and into the actual factory and service centers, where the automaker believes the tech can continue to improve on-the-floor productivity and guide its workers as they advance through their careers.

Recent findings suggest that decker says the AI can ingest and organize decades of institutional knowledge, making it accessible to workers during and beyond the training process. Scout has been feeding the AI equipment manuals and manufacturing documentation spanning multiple decades, disciplines and countries — what Decker called “hundreds of years of accumulated enterprise know-how” — which the AI earpiece can surface in real time, something he said was near impossible to do before in a world of binders and PDFs.

In a recent development, scout’s AI-fueled “passion project” arrives amid broader tensions across industries affected by artificial intelligence. Companies are eager for the efficiencies AI promises, while workers worry the same technology could eventually cost them their jobs. Scout’s executives didn’t address that concern directly in this exchange. Keogh framed the payoff in terms of speed — how promptly a newly introduced hire can be made productive — leaving the wider workforce conversation for another time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Signal is blocking screenshots inside its app on iOS 27, and on Android when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen.
  • Signal gave the post to Reuters ahead of its release, and Reuters’ Katie Paul reported the move first.
  • “Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Signal is blocking screenshots inside its app on iOS 27, and on Android when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen. The aim is to keep AI agents built into phone software away from private chats, Signal president Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post on Friday.

Signal gave the post to Reuters ahead of its release, and Reuters’ Katie Paul reported the move first.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission,” Whittaker wrote.

Recent findings suggest that her targets are Gemini Intelligence on Android and the Onscreen Awareness feature of Apple’s Siri AI. Both scan what is on the screen so they can answer questions and act for the user. Once captured, Signal data can end up in whatever local database or remote server the agent uses, outside Signal’s control, she wrote.

On iOS, a new “Block Siri AI” setting is on by default. Its description says it stops Siri AI from scanning Signal content and also blocks screenshots in the app and the App Switcher. On Android, Signal turns on its Screen security setting when an assistant tries to capture the screen.

Owners get pop-up windows that let them switch the block off, depending on the device, Reuters reported. Whittaker warned that doing so could expose their own and their contacts’ messages to the agents.

Recent findings suggest that she called the fix “incomplete”. Blocking screenshots does not stop agents from reaching content already stored on the phone through its filesystem.

It has been revealed that signal took the same step on Windows last year, against Microsoft’s Recall. It cannot do it on macOS. Apple, Google and Microsoft offer no easy way for apps to restrict AI data access without “drastic compromises” to how they work, Whittaker wrote. On a Mac, Signal suggests adding the app to the Excluded Apps list in the Siri settings, Digital Trends reported.

Signal asks for two things. Developers need an easy, documented way to opt their apps out of AI data access, from screen reading to files and notifications. The companies also need to explain how their agents access and process data. Confidential computing approaches “are not a complete solution”, Whittaker wrote.

Industry observers note that she also wants tools to rein in third-party agents such as Meta’s Muse. These use the deep permissions people grant them at setup. Such agents use accessibility settings as “a skeleton key”, she wrote.

Industry observers note that muse got around its own Connector tool to pull Signal messages on a Mac and on Android, Reuters reported earlier this week. On the Mac, it used accessibility and screenshot tools. An Apple update this week closed that route but added fresh agent permissions with extra warnings, according to Reuters.

It has been revealed that meta told Reuters that agents need to see and use people’s computers to work for them. Muse reaches other apps only through permissions users explicitly grant, it said. Meta has denied similar claims before.

Industry observers note that signal mentioned it is “cautiously optimistic” that Google and Apple are engaging with it on the problem. Whittaker has warned about agents since at least June.

“Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem,” the post mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cellular IoT has extended low-power connectivity to many remote places. Even so, about four-fifths of the earth’s surface remains outside the range of a base station. Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) address this gap by adding satellite access to the 5G standard. One modem can then connect through a satellite when no terrestrial cell is available.

Sources indicate that this shift changes how devices are designed. Satellites are in motion. Signals therefore face long propagation delays and changing Doppler shift. Link budgets are tight and device antennas are small. A device can pass static conformance tests and still fail on a real satellite link.

This White Paper explains these challenges. It also outlines the test conditions and measurements needed to evaluate synchronization, signaling, receiver performance, and link reliability.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The ribbon cutting at Mistral’s newly introduced Asia Pacific headquarters in Singapore.
  • Mistral AI is expanding its presence in Asia Pacific, opening a regional headquarters in Singapore that will double as a research hub for developing AI models tailored to local industries.
  • The French AI tech giant looks to build custom frontier models for three areas: public services, robotics, and high-tech manufacturing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The ribbon cutting at Mistral’s newly introduced Asia Pacific headquarters in Singapore.

Mistral AI is expanding its presence in Asia Pacific, opening a regional headquarters in Singapore that will double as a research hub for developing AI models tailored to local industries.

The French AI tech giant looks to build custom frontier models for three areas: public services, robotics, and high-tech manufacturing. It also wants to more than double its regional workforce, bringing the team to 200 people by 2027. Upcoming hires will work across research, applied AI, engineering, and robotics.

In a recent development, for Mistral, the Singapore office is about more than having a local presence. The tech giant wants to give governments and businesses in the region greater control over the AI systems they use.

“Our ambition is to establish Singapore as a strategic location for empowering governments and enterprises across Asia Pacific to retain ownership of their infrastructure and intelligence,” said Arthur Mensch, Mistral’s co-founder and chief executive.

It’s an argument Mistral has made repeatedly in Europe, where concerns about dependence on American technology have helped fuel interest in sovereign AI. Its open-weight models can be adapted and deployed within an organisation’s own infrastructure, allowing customers to retain control over their data and how the systems operate.

Singapore is a natural place to take that proposition further, as Mistral already has several partnerships in the city-state, including work with HTX, the Home Team Science and Technology Agency responsible for developing technology for Singapore’s public safety agencies.

In May 2025, HTX signed an agreement with Mistral and Microsoft to develop AI models for public safety applications. A strategic partnership with HTX followed, alongside collaborations with Singtel, NCS, and ST Engineering.

It has been revealed that the firm states its projects with HTX and DSO National Laboratories, Singapore’s defence research organisation, were among its first efforts to fine-tune models for individual customers. The experience also helped inform the development of its broader product portfolio.

For HTX, the collaboration has brought AI development closer to the operational needs of public safety agencies. Its chief AI officer, Ang Chee Wee, stated the partnership has allowed the organisation to ground its work in real-world operations.

Robotics is another area Mistral wants to develop from Singapore, as in July, the manufacturer released Robostral Navigate, an 8-billion-parameter model designed to help robots move through unfamiliar buildings using a single RGB camera. Mistral trained it entirely in simulation.

The new hub will build on that work, with research also covering physical AI and engineering simulations for manufacturing environments. These are areas where AI systems need to interact with the physical world, rather than process information or generate content.

In a recent development, founded in Paris in 2023, Mistral has become one of Europe’s most heavily funded AI companies, attracting investors as governments and businesses look for alternatives to US technology providers. Chip equipment maker ASML led its €1.7 billion Series C in September 2025, valuing the company at approximately €11.7 billion.

Singapore’s Economic Development Board welcomed the expansion, saying it would strengthen the country’s position in frontier AI and create opportunities for local talent to work on advanced AI research and development.

For Mistral, the move also gives it a stronger base in a region where governments are investing in their own AI capabilities. It also gives its European sovereignty pitch another market in which to prove itself.

At Scout Motors’ New Plant, Validation of Terra and Traveler EVs Has Begun

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (839 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At Scout Motors’ South Carolina Production Center, the automaker’s very first electrified trucks and SUVs are being welded, painted and assembled.
  • After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026.
  • I donned my hardhat, steel-toe caps and high-vis vest to get an early look inside the plant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At Scout Motors’ South Carolina Production Center, the automaker’s very first electrified trucks and SUVs are being welded, painted and assembled. The revived American automaker has begun the first validation builds of its upcoming Terra pickup truck and Traveler SUV at the Blythewood plant, but hold your electric horses — final production and customer deliveries are still a little over a year away.

After a period of slow sales, American interest in electric vehicles and hybrids is on the rise, driven by high fuel costs and the steady growth of EV charging infrastructure in 2026. Scout, with its battery-electric and gasoline range-extended powertrains, could have both of those bases covered when it arrives to compete in America’s most popular vehicle classes (trucks and SUVs) in 2028. It’s worth keeping an eye on Scout as it inches toward production.

I donned my hardhat, steel-toe caps and high-vis vest to get an early look inside the plant.

Industry observers note that the Volkswagen Group revived the Scout Motors brand (formerly International Scout) in 2022, and in 2024, the public got its first look at the Terra and Traveler concepts. The two were initially revealed as full-electric models with the option to add Scout’s Harvester onboard gasoline generator to boost the range.

However, demand for the extended-range EV configuration was overwhelming — roughly 87% of the 160,000-plus reservation holders selected the Harvester spec over the all-electric version — and Scout pivoted to delivering the EREV first, then following up with the pure battery-electric model later in production.

Both models are expected to start under $60,000, though Scout has not yet confirmed the exact price difference between the Harvester and pure BEV trims.

Sources indicate that in early 2024, the automaker broke ground on the Blythewood Production Center, pledging to invest more than $2 billion in the plant and create more than 4,000 local jobs. A year later, Scout confirmed plans to add a $300 million supplier park to the complex, supporting around 1,000 on-site jobs at parts suppliers.

Today, construction is mostly complete. (Executives told me it’s about 80% to 95% done, depending on how you measure it.) The walls are up, much of the equipment is in place, and the first movement toward full production of the brand’s extended-range EV and, eventually, battery electric trucks and SUVs has begun.

Scout’s manufacturing and production teams have begun building the first validation builds — early-stage preproduction vehicles that allow factory planners to dial in vehicle quality, confirm the accuracy of the engineering and hone the efficiency of the manufacturing and assembly lines.

According to recent reports, these aren’t complete vehicles by any stretch, being pulled from the line at various points to check and double-check that the fresh factory equipment functions properly and that the right parts arrive when and where they’re needed. Executives warned me that, at this point, there would still be inconsistencies as they dial in panel gaps, welds and the application of various coatings, but that Scout expects the process to be dialed in by the time full production starts in late 2027.

I was able to get up close to these validation vehicles, checking out a body-in-white bare chassis in the body shop, seeing various stages of coatings applied to bare metal, and watching workers complete calibration and alignment of lights and sensors in the final assembly area.

It has been revealed that along the way, Scout told me that more than 160 individual parts must come together to form the vehicle’s chassis, a process supported by more than 750 robots and 5,000 weld points. Once up to speed, the factory body shop is designed to produce around 40 vehicles per hour, with pickups and SUVs sharing the same line.

Industry observers note that however, while I saw the robotic welding arms and paint sprayers performing their motions to apply color, no vehicles were actually moving through the assembly line. This early in the process, the automaker doesn’t need a continuous flow of validation vehicles, and many of the factory areas — such as the supplier park that will provide the batteries, electric motors and modified VW Group four-cylinder engines for Harvester models — are still under construction.

Additionally, the validation process gives workers hands-on experience, rather than having them learn from mistakes on cars that will reach customers or being confined to a classroom.

As more parts of the factory complete construction and come online, the validation process will encompass more of the vehicle’s construction until the automaker is ready to start building full customer vehicles. Todd Johnson, Scout’s vice president of manufacturing, tells me that validation will continue into 2027 through multiple preproduction phases starting with the Traveler SUV.

The automaker expects the first customer deliveries of the Traveler Harvester to begin in early 2028, followed by the Terra Harvester and, eventually, fully electric versions of both.

It has been revealed that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Scout Motors. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Those came alongside several fresh features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing consumers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and owners on the public beta can now try out these upcoming features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, kirsten Davies, the Pentagon’s chief information officer, is replacing Sean Cairncross as the White House national cyber director.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Department of War Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies speaks at a CIO town hall at the Mark Center, Alexandria, Virginia, 10 February 2026.

According to recent reports, kirsten Davies, the Pentagon’s chief information officer, is replacing Sean Cairncross as the White House national cyber director. Axios first reported the change on Thursday, after a week of tech outages across the US.

Two White House officials told Axios that Stephen Miller, President Trump’s upcoming chief of staff, sought the change and pushed Cairncross out. One said Cairncross “lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job”. Two other sources described his departure to Axios as amicable.

A person close to the White House told Reuters’ Courtney Rozen that Cairncross was “fired”.

“The president fully supported firing Sean Cairncross from his position,” the person told Reuters.

Sources indicate that officials gave Semafor two versions. A White House official and a person familiar with the White House noted Trump backed his firing. Replacing him was one of Miller’s first tasks as chief of staff, the official said. A senior White House official and another person familiar with the matter disputed that. They told Semafor he resigned of his own accord.

Recent findings suggest that “It has been the honor of a lifetime to serve President Donald J. Trump,” Cairncross noted in a statement, quoted by Axios.

He had led the Office of the National Cyber Director, which coordinates cybersecurity policy across the federal government, since August 2025. His last public interview in the role was on stage at Semafor’s San Francisco event this week, Semafor said.

The change follows outages at Microsoft, US banks and the National Security Agency, and a nationwide ground stop that disrupted more than 18,000 flights, according to Reuters. Senior officials have said the outages had no common cause, and that no cyberattack lay behind them. Banks and the NSA reportedly blamed rushed security patches for some of them.

In a recent development, davies will take over temporarily, according to Reuters. A permanent national cyber director needs Senate confirmation. The Senate already confirmed Davies for the Pentagon role, Axios reported. Democrats take control of the Senate in January.

Before the Pentagon, Davies was chief information security officer at Unilever. She also held technology and cyber roles at Estée Lauder, Barclays Africa Group, Hewlett Packard and Siemens, according to her official biography.

She thanked Trump and Miller in a post on X late on Thursday.

According to recent reports, thank you @POTUS and @StephenM for your faith and steady confidence in me. And thank you @SecWar for your vigilant and visionary leadership.

Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected. Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come …but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on, as well as build cyber talent for our future. Under President Trump’s leadership we will have a more secure, resilient; and supercharged technological future.

I am honored to continue to serve.

– _Kirsten Davies_ (@_KirstenDavies_) November 20, 2026.

Cairncross’s team was already thinning. His former head of policy, Thomas Lind, left in June and joined OpenAI in October, Axios reported.

#4383. Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1184 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Ford Designed Its Fathom EV Battery Pack to Bend in a Crash, for Safety

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that ford’s newly introduced LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection.
  • In a recent development, conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish.
  • So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ford’s newly introduced LFP battery pack isn’t a fragile electric car component that needs protection. During my visit this week to the automaker’s newly operational battery plant, engineers proudly highlighted me a video of the battery being crash-tested, the shell and the prismatic cells within bending violently under the force. My jaw practically hit the floor.

In a recent development, conventional wisdom views an EV battery as a potentially explosive component that, if damaged, can cause catastrophic failure and hours-long fires that are difficult to extinguish. Years of lithium-ion batteries in phones, tablets and laptops taught us that and it’s largely held true for electric cars as well.

So the anxiety is well founded, even if, statistically, EVs are generally as safe as (if not safer than) internal combustion engine vehicles in crash testing and far less likely to catch fire.

Ford dropped that bombshell of a video on me at the end of my tour of its Blue Oval Battery Park outside Marshall, Michigan. However, I was barred from recording or photographing the footage.

Recent findings suggest that the design team’s mantra was “don’t assume a cell must never deform.” For the upcoming Fathom and Ford’s Universal EV platform, or UEV, the pack is designed to carry up to 40% of side-impact forces and is treated as part of the vehicle’s crash structure. The tech giant’s leadership and engineers are confident that the EV won’t catch fire or explode despite the bent cells.

“Traditionally the battery is thought of as payload, a fragile jewel you must protect,” mentioned Vladimir Bogachuk, chief engineer for advanced vehicle structure architecture at Ford. That approach, he said, means heavy bracing and protective structures around the pack. “The battery is not a jewel you must protect,” he said.

Sources indicate that bogachuk (along with every other Ford engineer and executive I spoke with that day) takes a less-is-more stance on the new EV platform. “The best part is no part,” he told me, “and if you have to have a part, it’s pretty much got to serve multiple functions.” And so the engineers set out to remove unnecessary armor and build a battery that serves double duty as an energy reservoir and crash structure.

Recent findings suggest that without that extra protection, the resulting EV can be lighter and more efficient, with improved driving dynamics. The UEV pack is deeply integrated into the vehicle’s structure: Its top lid is the cabin floor, and the seats bolt directly onto it. The bottom of the pack is the EV’s underbody. A service door beneath the Fathom’s rear seats will provide access to the charging and power electronics for service without the need to drop the pack.

It has been revealed that the crash videos highlighted deformation that would scare me on an older EV, but when I stopped to think, it wasn’t much different from what I’ve seen in conventional car side-impact crash tests. Ford notes an impact strong enough to deform the battery would also deform the chassis of a conventional vehicle or traditional EV, so the vehicle would likely be totaled anyway. More importantly, the engineers say the driver would be safe from thermal runaway and fire.

When asked, Ford’s engineers mentioned they don’t believe in a “right chemistry” for every electric vehicle. The UEV platform’s LFP — short for lithium iron phosphate — chemistry, prismatic cells and “jelly roll” construction were chosen for low manufacturing cost, resistance to temperature extremes, suitability for bidirectional energy use and the ability to deform while remaining inert under designed loads and forces.

Other automakers have floated solid-state batteries as a potential solution to battery safety and energy density, but the technology isn’t ready for use in production cars — at least not at the scale and price that Ford needs for the reasonably priced Fathom.

Industry observers note that ford hasn’t stated the LFP pack’s energy capacity, the cell capacity or the number of cells the Fathom’s pack will comprise. Based on a cutaway displayed during my tour, I estimate 90 to 108 individual prismatic cells. The aluminum prismatic cans that enclose the cathode-anode “jelly roll” battery provide structural support and aid thermal dissipation throughout the larger pack.

It has been revealed that wes Thibault, chief engineer for global energy storage systems, described the rigorous validation that the cells and packs underwent to reach the point where they can be trusted to bend like a taco. He told me that Ford has “a dedicated abuse-testing team” integrated with battery design and engineering at every level and stage of the manufacturing process, searching for edge cases and probing the limits of what the chemistry, the cells and full production-spec battery packs can take, from withstanding over 150,000 miles of simulated daily driving to remaining safe and inert in a crash. Along the way, CT scans of the cells offered an inside look at the jelly roll and how it was responding.

In a recent development, ford’s testing covers structural integrity and load-bearing capability, heat soak from minus 40 to 60 degrees Celsius, IP67 water resistance and humidity cycling, and high-charge and high-discharge tests. For multiaxis vibration, the battery, seats and brackets are strapped to what I can describe only as a giant mechanical bull that shakes the hardware through roll, pitch, yaw and multiple harmonic frequencies. Ford can combine multiple factors in a single test, such as a high-humidity heat soak under vibration during high discharge.

Once the first batch of UEV vehicles are on the road, Ford indicates it’ll be able to capture real-world data from the fleet to further fine-tune its validation methods for future generations of EVs.

Given how well the first model year of Ford’s Mustang Mach-E‘s batteries have held up after six years and thousands of real-world miles, it’s clear the automaker knows a thing or two about building a reliable battery.

Industry observers note that that stated, the UEV platform’s LFP chemistry and construction are very different from those of the earlier generation, and the automaker is asking much, much more of the pack than just holding and discharging energy. It’s asking the pack to actively protect the souls onboard in the event of a crash. Testing to failure early and learning from those mistakes promptly is something the engineers I spoke to seem to take very seriously.

This bold, out-of-the-box approach to how the automaker thinks about battery fragility — protecting the souls onboard rather than the “jewel” that is the battery from a potential crash at the end of the vehicle’s life — comes with the promise of more range and efficiency, less weight and more driving fun over the vehicle’s lifetime.

Sources indicate that I’m ready to believe. I want EV batteries to be safer and less scary. That promise depends heavily on whether the Fathom’s UEV battery pack is as safe as Ford notes it is when it reaches driveways and dealerships in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Ford. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

After 5 hours with GTA 6, I’ve already made 3 major mistakes — here’s how to avoid them

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1117 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait.
  • According to recent reports, like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro.
  • According to recent reports, so, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait. Not only is the Vice City map absolutely huge, but it’s the most system-rich and mechanically deep game in the Grand Theft Auto series to date. There’s an overwhelming amount of things to see, do, and learn.

According to recent reports, like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro. I’ve since put five hours of playtime into GTA 6, and while I’m still getting my head around all that the game has to offer (my completion percentage is a mere 12%), I’ve already learnt a few lessons the hard way. Yes, mistakes have been made.

According to recent reports, so, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free). Learn from my errors!

In a recent development, after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 introduces a new money system in which you can hold cash either on your person or stashed securely at your safehouse. If you get “wasted” or “busted” by the cops, you’ll lose all the money you’re carrying, but the funds kept under the floorboards at Jason's beachside home are protected.

As a cautious type, I took this to mean never carry any money on your person for fear of losing it, which pretty quickly proved to be an oversteer when an early mission required me to buy a gun, and I literally had $0 in my wallet. This forced a trip back to the safehouse, where I counted out the exact number of bills required to buy the weapon.

According to recent reports, once I returned to the Ammu-nation store, I bought my gun and then was presented with a range of attachments (some with a limited-time discount), which I couldn’t buy because, again, I’d only brought the specific amount required to buy the gun itself. Frustrating.

In a recent development, this taught me not to fear actually carrying money in your wallet. Sure, running about Vice City with your entire bank balance on hand is probably unwise, but you’re going to want, and need, some money in your pocket. At this early stage, I’ve been opting for a 50/50 split, keeping half my ill-gotten gains in my stash, and the other half within instant reach.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

My approach to previous GTA games tended to be this: Complete a few story missions, and then go on a psychotic rampage to blow off some steam (I swear I’m not a total psycho).

GTA 6 is different. For pretty much the first time in the franchise’s history, the game actively discourages you from causing carnage without purpose through the new “Criminal Profile” system. Your in-game actions are tracked and contribute to the type of criminal Jason (and later Lucia) is becoming. Ranging from a “professional” all the way to a full-blown “psycho.”.

During my first GTA 6 session, after completing the mandatory prologue, I decided to see how many wanted stars I could rack up with just the starter pistol, and pretty swiftly the game warned me that my criminal spree would have consequences. It felt like that old Tellale’s The Walking Dead warning message, “Clementine will remember that…”.

Rockstar has confirmed your “Criminal Profile” will impact how the story plays out, and I certainly don’t want to receive a “bad” ending; such was my concern about how my early game rampage would impact how my GTA 6 story plays out, I opted to reload to a previous save to instantly wash away the worrying amount of blood already on Jason’s hands.

In a recent development, so, in GTA 6, it pays to show restraint. You will commit many crimes, of course, but resist the urge to go full GTA and instead commit your criminal acts with purpose and even planning.

Sources indicate that speaking of planning, from what I’ve played so far, GTA 6 is the most ambitious Grand Theft Auto yet in all areas, including mission design. Previous GTA games present players with cinematic but largely linear missions; if you tried to get creative, the game would promptly shepherd you back onto the golden path with instant fail states for any deviations.

To be clear, GTA 6 does have these types of missions as well, but there’s a larger focus on player choice and letting you pick your approach. As an early (spoiler-free) example, a Chapter 1 mission asks you to retrieve a red sports car from a police impound lot.

You’re dropped off right outside the main gate, with an on-screen prompt encouraging you to break the lock. Naturally, I obliged, and the impound’s alarms started blaring; every cop in the area was instantly alerted, and the mission pretty much went further south from there.

In a recent development, one reload later, I was back at the mission start, and this time, I slowed down. I cased the joint first, walking the perimeter, trying to find a subtler way to access the impound lot. And what do you know, a conveniently placed scissor lift around the corner got me onto the roof, allowing me to quietly drop into the compound without setting off any alarms or alert cops.

It’s a reminder that in GTA 6, thinking before you act can pay off, and when you factor in the “Criminal Profile” system, there is real merit in completing missions without having to shoot your way out of trouble.

Linq raises $90M to give AI assistants a phone and a computer

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Linq co-founders Elliott Potter, Patrick Sullivan and Jared Mattsson.
  • If you ask your AI to move your dentist appointment, it will likely draft a note for you to send to them, but stop there.
  • To effectively handle the request, the assistant would need to send a text, make a call, or use their website.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Linq co-founders Elliott Potter, Patrick Sullivan and Jared Mattsson.

If you ask your AI to move your dentist appointment, it will likely draft a note for you to send to them, but stop there.

To effectively handle the request, the assistant would need to send a text, make a call, or use their website.

Sources indicate that linq wants to give AI assistants those tools. The startup announced this week that to help build that infrastructure, it just raised $90 million in a round led by Andreessen Horowitz, along with TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, Abstract, Anthos and Left Lane Capital.

Sources indicate that its pitch to developers is simple. They can give an assistant a phone to text and call people, plus a computer to use websites and software on a user’s behalf.

The firm also announced that Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz’s co-founder and general partner, is joining its board.

Recent findings suggest that message-based personal assistants that can take actions on your behalf are among the hottest verticals in AI right now. There’s no new interface to learn, and the request can be as specific as you like. “Friday after 3, preferably at the same office” is easier to type than it is to translate into a series of searches, filters, and phone calls.

Recent findings suggest that what makes the idea interesting for Linq is that the person sending that text and the business receiving the request may have very different preferences. You might want to handle the whole thing by message. Your dentist’s receptionist might be perfectly happy to help, provided someone picks up the phone.

Linq started with the texting side of that equation. The firm claims it has processed more than 1 billion messages across customers including DoorDash, Town, Tomo, and hundreds of others. DoorDash uses Linq to let customers find food, build a cart, and check out in a single message thread.

Its new voice product, called HD Calling for Agents, adds another option for developers. An assistant could take instructions over text and use a voice call for the part of the job that requires one. For the person who asked to move the appointment, the appeal is fairly mundane. They can go back to what they were doing and wait for a text telling them which time is available.

Recent findings suggest that then there are the tasks that require someone to sit down at a computer. Linq’s computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure where they can interact with software. For a developer building a personal assistant, that opens up a different set of jobs, particularly when a business has a website people can use but no convenient way for another application to complete the same task.

It has been revealed that “Clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent: ‘pay rent,’” Linq CEO Elliott Potter mentioned in the announcement. “We help developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work.”.

The combination becomes more interesting when a task moves between channels. A receptionist might agree to a new appointment by phone, then send a link to a form that has to be completed before the booking is final. A voice-only assistant would have to hand the job back at that point. One with access to messaging and a computer could finish it.

In a recent development, linq’s bet gives it some distance from one of the biggest questions around personal AI assistants. Will people want one general-purpose assistant that handles everything from takeout to rent, or will they use different agents provided by the businesses they already know? Linq has a potential customer in either case. Both kinds of developers need ways for their software to reach people and get things done.

Sources indicate that “Agents will communicate and get work done just like people do,” Horowitz said in the announcement. “Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale.”.

If personal AI assistants catch on, the phone in your pocket could become the place you hand off an errand you’d otherwise spend your lunch break doing. You text what you need. Your assistant calls the office, works through the booking system, and gets back to you with a confirmed time. Linq’s $90 million bet is that as more people come to expect that kind of help, the developers building their assistants will need a phone and a computer for each one.

#4377. GTA 6’s 30 FPS lock broke my PC gamer brain — until I turned on the one TV setting I swore I’d never touch

📖 Baca

GTA 6’s 30 FPS lock broke my PC gamer brain — until I turned on the one TV setting I swore I’d never touch

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve ever bought a fresh TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.
  • According to recent reports, for movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder.
  • And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever bought a fresh TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.

According to recent reports, for movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder. I hate it. Tom Cruise hates it. You should hate it too.

And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.

Industry observers note that to understand how I ended up committing TV heresy, you have to understand the shock to the system that is GTA 6’s frame rate. Coming straight from my monster PC rig playing games like Resident Evil Requiem at up to 214 FPS, dropping back down to a strict 30 FPS console lock feels like wading through treacle.

According to recent reports, but on top of that, as I’ve seen (and you’ve seen on Digital Foundry’s test), that 30 FPS lock isn’t an actual lock. It can dip into the mid-20s during heavy scenes. Coming from super fluidity, that 30 FPS is brutal to adapt to.

So out of sheer desperation (and because we’re stuck waiting for the PC port), I broke the golden rule and toggled my TV’s smooth motion setting on.

And I hate to admit it, but it’s basically bootleg DLSS Frame Generation for your living room.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Just like PC frame generation tricks of old, your TV’s motion interpolation processor looks at two real frames from your console, guesses what should happen in between them, and inserts an artificial frame to smooth out the motion.

Industry observers note that the moment I flipped it on in GTA 6, that nauseating camera stutter when cruising down Ocean Beach vanished. Panning around a crowded street or taking a high-speed corner suddenly felt dramatically more fluid — nowhere near 60 fps, and definitely not my desktop rig, but miles smoother than the choppy presentation.

Sources indicate that before the AV forums come for my head with pitchforks, let’s be completely honest about the trade-offs. There is no such thing as a free lunch in frame interpolation:.

Industry observers note that because your TV has to wait for the next frame before it can invent the one in the middle, motion smooth adds latency between pressing a button and seeing the result on screen. In twitchy, competitive games, that’s a death sentence.

But in a Rockstar open-world game — where character movement is already famously weighty and deliberate — I never noticed that extra latency.

Your TV’s processor is just guessing after all, and while it is a good guesser, there are some moments of weird shimmering around fast-moving objects and some boiling around on-screen elements like subtitles. Probably compounded by the fact GTA 6 is already running its own resolution scaling tech under the hood.

Standard Game Mode and VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) automatically lock out motion smoothing on many TVs. Depending on your set, you either have to turn on the dedicated low-latency Game Motion Plus mode (found on newer Samsung and LG sets) or sacrifice VRR to unlock it.

The silver lining, though, is that with this being a 30 FPS game, it’s not high enough to require VRR anyway.

If GTA 6’s 30 FPS cap is giving your eyes a workout and you want to test the dark arts yourself, don’t just blindly max out every slider.

If your TV has a low-latency interpolation option (like Samsung’s Game Motion Plus or LG’s TruMotion tweaks), use that before turning off Game Mode completely.

Sources indicate that set Judder Reduction to a middle ground (around 5-7 out of 10) rather than maxing it out. You want to take the harsh edge off camera pans without turning your car into a blurry smudge.

This is optional based on personal taste. Test how your TV’s smoothing looks with GTA’s built-in motion blur turned off. For a lot of OLED owners, letting the TV handle the smoothing cleanly beats stacking two different blur effects on top of each other.

Do I want to play GTA 6 at native 240 FPS on my PC rig? Obviously. The second Rockstar drops the PC version, I’ll be uninstalling this hack from my brain and never looking back.

I still wouldn’t be caught dead watching a movie with motion smoothing turned on. But until PC gamers get their turn in Vice City, breaking the ultimate TV rule is the best survival trick I’ve found for making a 30 FPS masterpiece actually feel better to play.

Also yes, my wife has taken note of the fact that I share the same name as the male protagonist. And yes, she is side-eyeing how I treat Lucia hard.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a great day for designers who hate AI. Canva, the online design and publishing platform, announced on Thursday that it’s introducing two fresh settings to opt out of seeing and using AI tools. One lets you turn off AI tools in Canva, and the other lets you filter out AI-created content from Canva’s library of templates and other elements.

It has been revealed that the settings are available now for free and paying users globally, except for those in India, the Philippines and Indonesia. Canva administrators for business and team plans can enable the two new settings for their entire organization.

According to recent reports, to turn off Canva’s AI, go to your Profile > Settings > Preferences and toggle Enable generative AI features on or off. To filter out AI in your Canva library, go to Profile > Your account > AI personalization and enable the feature that claims show less AI-generated content.

Industry observers note that it’s hard not to compare Canva’s newly introduced opt-out features to Adobe, which spent all of last week at Adobe Max trying to convince creative professionals to embrace its AI tools. Adobe’s chief technology officer told CNET that he thought the problem was slop, not AI.

Industry observers note that as criticisms of AI mount, it’s smart, albeit rare, to see a tech company give its people a definitive, one-click solution to filter out AI tools. We will have to put Canva’s settings to the test to see how effectively they work, though.

Sources indicate that if you do want to use AI, Canva has no shortage. Its magic layers tool lets you break apart an AI-generated image into editable layers, a hugely helpful capability for fixing errors and customizing content. Its foundational models, along with other third-party models, can help you generate fresh image, video and audio content. Outside of graphic design, Canva has added AI tools for spreadsheet, document and presentation work over the past year. And like every other tech organization, Canva indicates it looks to continue investing in AI.

Apple store in Sanlitun, Beijing.

Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported on Thursday. It would write code, browse the web, control apps and move around devices for users. The report is based on job listings Apple added to its careers site this week.

One listing seeks a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. Apple has eyed a launch as soon as the end of 2027, according to Bloomberg. Development is still at an early stage.

“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the listing reads.

The agents would proposal and carry out multistep tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code and APIs. They could also coordinate specialised subagents, the listing says. It also names “general-purpose computer-use agents”. That kind of tool already lets ChatGPT and Meta’s Muse operate a Mac.

Agents that run code, use credentials and act for consumers need “strong permission models, sandboxing and transparency”, it adds.

Apple appears to have pulled the listing, Digital Trends reported. A screenshot shared on X matches its role number and its 17 November posting date. The role did not appear in a search of Apple’s careers site on Friday. The hire would work with Apple’s Siri, UI Frameworks and Apple Foundation Models teams, Digital Trends reported.

Apple’s fresh chief executive, John Ternus, has been pressing Craig Federighi to move faster on AI. An agent is central to that push, according to Bloomberg.

Apple is also making it harder for other companies’ agents to control a Mac. In the macOS 27.3 beta, turning on ChatGPT’s computer-use support takes 14 steps, up from four, Bloomberg reported. New warning screens ask consumers to reconsider granting third-party agents that control.

Apple presents the change as a way to protect users. Some AI companies and users see it as an attempt to slow competitors, according to Bloomberg. In October, Apple noted AI agents were the reason for new Full Disk Access controls on Macs.

According to recent reports, openAI launched its Dots agents in September, and Anthropic previewed Duet in October. Gemini on the Mac gained computer use on Thursday.

Meta shares fell nearly 2% and Anthropic’s more than 3% in late trading after the report, Bloomberg noted.

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp people: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

Recent findings suggest that whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the newly introduced limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

Industry observers note that this rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the manufacturer announced four upcoming features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

#4371. iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1969 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

iPhone Duo, One Month Later: I’m Not Ready to End the Love Affair

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1969 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review.
  • Apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done.
  • Still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One month after getting the iPhone Duo, I’ve stuck to my commitment to keep using it even after publishing my review. Well, mostly.

Apple’s debut foldable has proven to be a practical everyday device, whether I’m streaming movies, texting or getting work done. I’ve grown so accustomed to using it that I sometimes forget how much attention it draws when I pull it out of my pocket, especially given its limited availability and lengthy preorder windows – not to mention its sky-high $1,999 starting price.

Still, there have been times when I’ve reached for the iPhone 18 Pro Max instead for its more advanced camera system, as well as its familiar, straightforward design. The Duo’s cameras pull their weight with casual photography, but while filming social content at F1’s US Grand Prix and chatting with filmmakers at an SFFilm screening, I couldn’t resist going for the best cameras at my disposal on the Pro Max. There are times a conventional slab phone just does the trick – without all the frills and novelty of a folding one.

In a recent development, that hasn’t stopped me from keeping the Duo as my primary device. It’s an enjoyable phone to use, with its compact, palm-sized build and spacious inner display. Plus, as CNET’s ongoing folding test demonstrates, it has a durable build that ensures I can fold and unfold it to my heart’s content.

And if I’m being honest, I kind of love how much of a statement piece it’s become.

Sources indicate that the Duo’s versatility has really shown its appeal the more I live with it. I find myself using the 5.4-inch cover screen and 7.6-inch inner display pretty equally, demonstrating the practicality of each.

When I’m on the move, the cover screen suffices for sending texts, responding to emails and checking notifications. Lounging around at home, I’m more inclined to use the larger inner display to endlessly scroll through Instagram or binge YouTube videos.

According to recent reports, the matte inner display remains one of my favorite elements. It reduces the appearance of the crease as well as glare, making it easier to see content even outdoors. Yes, the coating can dim the vibrant colors in images and videos, even with the screen’s 3,000-nit peak brightness, and smudges become prominent. But I can live with both of those drawbacks, and a microfiber cloth fixes the latter.

Apple’s phone-tablet hybrid came in clutch when I was on a recent flight and didn’t want to pull out my laptop. Instead, I used the Duo’s split-screen mode to place the Notes app on one half of the screen and an informational video on the other so I could quickly jot down the main points. The Duo has also become my gym buddy; I prop it open on the treadmill so I can watch Magpie Murders on a tablet-like display, then fold it up and toss it in my pocket when I’m done.

It has been revealed that apple Pencil support really helps the Duo feel like a mini iPad, and the matte coating on the inner display adds a satisfying resistance that more closely emulates the feel of writing on paper than a glossy surface. It gives jotting down notes, highlighting book passages and marking up documents a more tactile feel. I’m not much of a doodler, but I imagine that’s fun, too.

It has been revealed that the Apple Pencil can magnetically attach to the outer surface of the hinge, though it definitely sticks out, so there’s not really a practical, secure way to carry it around with the Duo (at least not that Apple has shared, but case-makers are sure to cook up a solution). I’m glad the stylus also works on the Duo’s cover screen, though the smaller size and glossy display make that experience slightly less satisfying.

According to recent reports, the number of apps optimized for the Duo at launch was relatively small, but it’s steadily increased. I gasped aloud on the train platform one morning while sending an email, realizing Gmail had finally been adapted for the Duo. It’s refreshing to see apps that feel intentional and fill the screen, rather than being awkwardly letterboxed.

Industry observers note that apple said in early November that more than 100,000 apps built for the iPhone Duo were live in the App Store. A week later, that number ballooned to over 200,000 apps. So despite a rather slow start, virtually all apps I regularly use now work seamlessly on Apple’s foldable.

One of my favorite apps on the Duo is Instagram’s Edits. When holding the phone open in landscape orientation, I can view the video timeline and make edits on the right side of the screen while seeing a preview of the video on the left. Rotated to portrait orientation, the layout resembles the interface on a traditional smartphone, but on a larger scale, which is helpful especially for making smaller tweaks.

It’s great to see more apps that don’t just expand to the larger screen, but make meaningful use of the Duo’s design.

It has been revealed that as I found during my review, the Duo’s battery life has been pretty good. It consistently lasts through the day, even as I hop between displays. I usually charge my phone at night, but even if I don’t, I know I’ll have some remaining battery in the morning.

According to recent reports, for instance, one day I started at 6:30 a.m. with a full battery. After my usual routine of checking emails, texting, scrolling through social media and browsing YouTube throughout the day, my battery was at 55% by 9:12 p.m. The next morning, I woke up with 48% battery, and that charge lasted through a similar routine, along with phone calls, texting and music and video streaming, before the battery finally died at 7:30 p.m.

The Duo has yet to give me a reason to stress about its battery life.

It has been revealed that I will acknowledge I’m a tad pretentious when it comes to smartphone cameras. But if I’m documenting an event or photographing my fancy tea sets, I want the best cameras I can get. Unlike the Duo, iPhone 18 Pro models have a telephoto camera, more advanced optical zoom capabilities and larger main-camera sensors.

Most of the time, the Duo’s 48-megapixel wide and ultrawide cameras do the trick just fine. Colors are vivid, details are sharp and images are bright. Videos look good, too, though the 18 Pro Max does a noticeably better job with nighttime footage, which can look more muddy on the Duo. Digital video on the Duo also tops out at 6x, versus 24x on the Pros. Most of the time, though, I’m quite content with what I capture with the Duo’s cameras.

Industry observers note that as I noted in my review, the under-display FaceTime camera on the inner screen isn’t great, but I never really take selfies using that camera. It feels much more natural to use the 12-megapixel selfie camera on the cover screen, which serves up sharp photos every time.

Recent findings suggest that the cover screen selfie camera plays a critical role in an patch that makes using the Duo even more seamless. In its latest iOS 27.3 developer beta, Apple added an option to unlock the iPhone Duo using the front camera.

In the absence of Face ID, which I have felt rather painfully, this has been a solid workaround, even if it’s not as secure as Apple’s biometric facial recognition and authentication system. You’ll still need to use Touch ID or a passcode when using Apple Pay or accessing passwords, and to unlock the phone after leaving it alone for around 45 minutes. But a win is a win. (You can also unlock the Duo using an Apple Watch, but I don’t have one.).

According to recent reports, I’ll admit I still feel a little bashful when pulling out the Duo because of how much attention it drums up, despite being far from the first foldable phone. But its limited availability and hype paired with the unique design make it eye-catching, for better or worse. Using the Duo has led to some fun conversations, whether it’s with a sales associate as I pay for a pastry or with Project Hail Mary directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller, who spotted the phone in my hand during an interview and geeked out over it. That’s been a fun side effect of using Apple’s first foldable in my everyday life.

I’ve been living dangerously without a case; I don’t want anything to detract from the phone’s sleek feel. This is one of those “do as I say, not as I do” moments, as I’d recommend slapping a case on a phone that costs nearly $2,000. I did put a tempered glass screen protector on the cover display to guard against scratches. I can feel its edge against the otherwise flush surface of the phone when I hold it open, but aesthetic sacrifices must be made.

The Duo isn’t perfect, even if I love using this phone. After holding Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, the iPhone Duo can feel slightly chunky. The Z Fold 8 measures 4.5mm thick when open and 9.7mm when closed. Meanwhile, the Duo is 5.2mm thick when open and 11.3mm when closed. It’s not a huge difference, but it makes me look forward to Apple hopefully slimming down the second-generation version, if and when it comes.

The Duo is also slightly heavier than the Z Fold 8, weighing 254 grams (compared to 201 grams for Samsung’s foldable). I’m always surprised when people remark how heavy the Duo is, but I think the reason I don’t share that sentiment is that I’m accustomed to the iPhone 18 Pro Max, which weighs 249 grams.

In a recent development, when the Duo is open in landscape orientation, I’m glad there’s an option to split the keyboard so it’s easier to type across the wider expanse, but I wish the swipe functionality worked in that configuration, too. It’s a little thing that would make a noticeable difference for those of us who rely heavily on swipe-to-text.

One drawback of the Duo’s compact design is that some existing MagSafe wallets and other accessories won’t stick to the back without awkwardly jutting out. So you might have to invest in some upcoming accessories specifically designed for the Duo.

Until the recent addition of face unlock, the Duo’s biggest drawback was the lack of Face ID. It’s a feature I’d expect on such a premium device, especially given that even the budget-focused iPhone 17E supports it.

Industry observers note that touch ID works reliably on the Duo, but it’s slow compared to fingerprint unlock on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which also supports facial recognition). And while the new face unlock capability on the Duo isn’t an exact replacement for Face ID, which is more secure, it helps make accessing the phone’s contents more convenient and in line with the Duo’s modern aesthetics.

It has been revealed that I’ve finished my homework: My review is done, and now, so is this one-month follow-up. What’s next?

Sources indicate that I’m not sure I’m ready to throw in the towel on Apple’s foldable just yet. The novelty of the iPhone Duo hasn’t worn off, and I’ve become quite used to my passport-size companion. It does just about everything I need, despite some slight imperfections, and it’s fun to use. It’s also amusing to see how people react when they see it in my hand.

So for now, it looks like the Duo will remain my daily driver. Whether the honeymoon phase eventually wears off remains to be seen, but I’m not in any hurry to end this love affair.
