    Our Readers Say This Is the Laptop Brand to Shop for During Black Friday Sales

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums.
    • Sources indicate that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics.
    • Apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple customers saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Holiday sales like Black Friday and Cyber Monday usually have good personal tech deals on TVs, wearables and robot vacuums. It’s also a good time to shop for a new laptop, but not every brand is worth your time and money.

    Sources indicate that we recently surveyed CNET readers as part of our People’s Picks awards to get their opinion on their laptop brand — including their take on its battery life, durability and performance for gaming and graphics. Our readers could choose from many popular laptop brands, but one was a clear favorite. It claimed eight awards, including the overall winner for CNET’s People’s Pick award. And it’s the one worth heavily considering if you plan to buy a fresh laptop while there are holiday savings.

    Apple wins the overall award in CNET’s People’s Picks, and also takes home the overall satisfaction rating, with 74.2% of Apple customers saying they’re extremely satisfied with their laptop. In comparison, 22.5% say they’re satisfied — bringing Apple to a near-perfect overall satisfaction score of 96.7%.

    According to recent reports, apple’s overall impression also speaks to other awards it wins from CNET readers, including high ratings for its impressive battery life, display quality and high-quality build. All of those categories and more sum up Apple’s brand loyalty nod, with 68% of MacBook owners saying they would buy the same laptop and model from Apple again.

    In a recent development, how much are people paying for MacBooks? CNET found that 43.5% of Apple customers paid at least $1,500. Until earlier in 2026, the MacBook Air was Apple’s entry-level laptop, priced at least $1,299. The introduction of the budget-friendly MacBook Neo brought that down to a more reasonable $699. However, despite Apple’s laptops being more expensive than those from other brands, they still ranked high for their value proposition. Part of the reason for that is that MacBooks received high marks for hardware reliability. “Apple’s MacBooks might cost more than the average laptop, but their premium build quality means they’re built for the long haul,” remarked Matt Elliott, CNET’s laptop editor.

    If you blueprint to have your laptop for a while, you may be impressed by other features that make work easier and faster, like its M-series central processing unit for task management and AI capabilities, great battery life and a one-of-a-kind operating system — right now MacOS 27. All of the features and specifications bundled together make Apple’s perception as a high-end laptop worth the investment for long-term satisfaction.

    According to recent reports, apple clinches a near-perfect score for its value perception. According to our survey results, 44% of Apple users said their MacBook has exceptional value. Others say their MacBook is worth what they paid for it (50.9%) — for a total positive score of 94.6%.

    Digging deeper into Apple’s cost-to-value rating, 81.8% of Apple owners paid at least $1,000 for their laptops, which may seem costly, but Apple users seem OK with the price. That could be because, even though Apple has only three laptop models in a handful of sizes in its lineup, each one delivers solid performance and storage.

    Take Apple’s proprietary processing chips, for example — each upgrade since the M1 release has improved the laptop’s speed, battery life and performance. Now the M6 can handle the MacBook’s AI capabilities, storage and high-resolution graphics. And for all of that power, most MacBooks are relatively thin and lightweight, making them easier for mobility — just a few of the reasons Apple owners may be OK with paying more for what they’re getting.

    Battery life is a big deal for many laptop buyers, and that’s another area where Apple delivers. Over a quarter of those surveyed (25.7%) said their MacBook’s battery life exceeds 10 hours — which is more than enough for a full day of work in most cases. And 18.7% say their MacBook’s battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours — totaling 44.4% of MacBook consumers saying their battery lasts 8 hours or more.

    Sources indicate that comparatively, non-Apple laptop brands fall short in this category. Only 16.4% of Lenovo customers say their laptop’s battery lasts at least 8 hours, and even fewer for Dell (12.7%) and HP (11.8%). If you’re leaning toward a MacBook for its battery life, CNET’s lab test reveals that the MacBook Neo lasts 13 hours and 26 minutes for online streaming, whereas the Apple MacBook Air 13-inch M5 (2026 model) lasts 17 hours and 2 minutes.

    Sources indicate that apple sweeps the brightness, color accuracy and clarity category with 99.2% of its users either satisfied or extremely satisfied with their laptop’s screen performance. No Apple users reported dissatisfaction.

    It has been revealed that “Apple has long been a favorite for creative professionals and content creators for good reason: Its MacBook displays are some of the best you’ll find on any laptop,” noted Josh Goldman, CNET’s managing editor for computers. “While Apple may use marketing names like Retina and Liquid Retina to describe display features, they do translate into sharp and clear text and images, with excellent brightness, contrast, color gamut coverage and color accuracy.”.

    Industry observers note that the new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR even goes beyond what MacBook users have come to expect. It’s Apple’s first OLED touchscreen laptop and features next-level brightness, color and contrast.

    Apple receives high ratings: 80% of MacBook owners say it has premium build quality, 18.2% say it’s solid, and those results don’t surprise us.

    It has been revealed that and MacBooks seem durable and reliable, with 87% of Apple users reporting no hardware failures on their MacBooks, while 8% say minor software fixes resolved their issues. Only 3% needed minor hardware repairs, and 2.2% needed major repairs — which could be fixes such as a battery or screen replacement.

    According to recent reports, our editors say the M5 MacBook Air is thin and lightweight, but still has a well-built aluminum design. And the M5 Pro MacBook Pro is sturdy, too. What sets Apple’s laptop hardware apart could be its aluminum chassis — the casing that holds all of the components together.

    “Apple makes three lines of MacBooks — the Neo, Air and Pro — and focuses on making those the best they can possibly be. They are all built to deliver a premium experience using high-quality materials, and that even includes the entry-level MacBook Neo,” stated Goldman.

    It has been revealed that lastly, Apple uses durable materials, such as the 100% recycled aluminum alloy it says encloses the 14-inch MacBook Pro. And the tech giant has several testing facilities to test MacBook durability.

    When it comes to getting your daily tasks done, most CNET readers with MacBooks (70.9%) say Apple’s laptops handle workloads flawlessly. It’s worth noting that 45% use their MacBook for work tasks, but no Apple users reported poor performance.

    It has been revealed that here’s why that might be: Apple’s laptops are packed with top-notch performance specs and features, like their powerful processors, unified memory and fast storage. Better processor performance means enhanced graphics, on-device AI capabilities and faster task speeds, all of which add up to being able to finish work, play games or stream videos without concerns or lags caused by your laptop’s hardware.

    On the software side, MacOS 27 Golden Gate gives you built-in AI features, like Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. And you can organize your Safari tabs by topic and use the Notify Me tool to be notified of website changes, like price drops or breaking news. Plus, you can create shortcuts to automate tasks. Coupling all of these features and specifications explains why Apple people rate MacBooks so highly for getting the job done.

    In a recent development, apple leads the way on brand retention with 68% of Apple people planning to buy the same MacBook model again, while 29.1% would buy another model from Apple’s lineup. Only 3% would switch to another brand that’s not Apple.

    In a recent development, usually, when you buy one Apple product, you’re likely to stick to the brand’s ecosystem, especially since Apple has its own operating systems to access its unique features and work seamlessly with other Apple products with Apple’s Continuity feature. For example, you can start an email on your iPhone, but finish typing it on your MacBook. Or you can call or send a text from your laptop without reaching for your iPhone. Other features work across Apple devices, including iCloud, Universal Clipboard and AirDrop.

    Asus wins as a midtier laptop choice with 67% of Asus owners paying between $500 and $1,499. There’s a sweet spot in this range with 38% spending between $500 and $999, and 28% paying between $1,000 and $1,499.

    If you’re planning to spend that amount on a upcoming laptop, you may also be pleased to know that Asus earns a higher satisfaction rating compared with other non-Apple laptop brands — 48% of Asus people say they’re extremely satisfied.

    Asus laptops have a few features and specifications that may speak to that rating, regardless of budget. For example, the Zenbook A14 has a thin, lightweight design that’s rigid, with long battery life and an OLED display with strong contrast and color performance. This Copilot Plus PC sells for $1,600 (but retailers like Best Buy regularly have it on sale for less). Comparatively, these premium features from other brands could cost more or sacrifice important must-have features for the price.

    Asus has other laptops worth exploring depending on your needs, like the budget-friendly Asus ZenBook S 14 or the premium Asus ROG Zephyrus G14 that could be good for gamers and creators.

    Industry observers note that over one-third of Acer laptop owners (38%) paid less than $500 for their laptop — which is greater than other laptop brands in this price range. Yet, 44% of Acer users say their laptop has exceptional value, while 50% say the value is fair — bringing a total positive cost-to-value score of over 94%. Acer also has an overall satisfaction score of 92.6% — the highest of non-Apple laptop brands.

    If you’re impressed by Acer’s value and satisfaction scores, there are a few budget-friendly Acer options to consider. The Acer Aspire 16 AI wins CNET’s Editors’ Choice award. It has a substantial 16-inch screen but is still lightweight (3.5 pounds). And it has good battery life (over 21 hours on CNET’s battery drain test). There are a few other pluses, like the 1440p web camera that may be good for video conferencing and a sizable touchpad. All of those features and more add up to $700, which could make it a good computer for work or casual browsing. If you’re looking to spend slightly less, its predecessor, the Aspire 14 AI, is originally $639, but you may be able to score deals on both models during holiday sales.

    Even though Apple is highly recommended by CNET readers, there are plenty of other laptop models and brands worth considering depending on your needs. Here are a few non-Apple laptop brands that are runner-ups to CNET’s People’s Picks winners that you shouldn’t count out of your laptop search.

    In a recent development, lenovo is best known for packing a powerful laptop into a compact design with tablet functionality, like its Yoga line, and its durable ThinkPad business models. But CNET readers with Lenovo laptops say the brand’s battery life stands out most compared with other non-MacBook laptops.

    Survey findings show that 16% of Lenovo owners say their laptops can run for 8 hours or more. And 10.5% say their laptop battery lasts between 8 and 10 hours, while 6% say their Lenovo laptops can withstand at least 10 hours before needing a charge. That’s more than what readers say about other non-Apple brands. The Yoga 9i 2-in-1 Aura Edition lasts 25 hours and 45 minutes — making it one of the best laptop batteries CNET experts have tested.

    Goldman remarked Lenovo has such a large and varied PC selection using the latest chips from Intel, AMD, Qualcomm and Nvidia that there is something for everyone and every budget. Even those who spend less on a Lenovo laptop can expect solid performance, including battery life.

    It has been revealed that if your laptop’s hardware fails or it breaks, you may be in the market for a latest laptop sooner than expected. Think about cooling fan problems, overheating or your laptop not powering on at all. Over half (68%) of Lenovo laptop owners said they haven’t had any hardware problems with their laptops — the most compared to other non-MacBooks.

    Beyond hardware durability, Lenovo also scores highly for its build and construction — overall making it a sturdy laptop choice. In our survey, 38% of Lenovo laptop owners say their laptop has a premium feel, while 51% say it’s solid — totaling a positive score of 89%.

    Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for recommendations, the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 has an all-metal design. And the Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 is a business laptop with Lenovo’s well-known X1 Carbon exterior and upcoming Space Frame design, which Elliott states makes it easier to repair or replace parts if needed.

    Many Lenovo laptop users are loyal to the brand, which speaks to the overall positive satisfaction rating of 83%. If Lenovo owners were in the market for a newly introduced laptop, nearly three in four (73.2%) say they would buy another Lenovo laptop. Breaking down the percentage, 33.6% say they would buy the same model again. Meanwhile, 39.6% would buy a different model but stick to Lenovo.

    It has been revealed that here’s why that might be. Lenovo offers a plethora of options to choose from based on your needs — while still evolving its laptops. For instance, the Lenovo Legion 5i Gen 10 has an open M.2 slot for a second storage drive and an OLED screen for crisp, colorful images — making it perfect for gaming. Its Yoga two-in-ones let you seamlessly switch between a tablet and traditional laptop, while Lenovo’s ThinkPad and ThinkBook business laptops offer everything from ultralight 2-pound bodies to expanding rollable screens. And its fresh designs don’t sacrifice the must-have needs like long battery life, durability and chip efficiency that lend to strong performance.

    Asus wins over nearly half of its laptop owners, with 47.5% giving it an exceptional value rating  — exceeding expectations for its price. Take our Editors’ Choice pick, the Asus Zenbook A14. It’s super thin and lightweight, but it’s still sturdy thanks to its Ceralumnium body. Plus, it has supreme 24-hour battery life, 1TB of storage and an OLED display — all for $1,200. While that’s more expensive than some laptops, it’s what’s included in that price that makes it worthwhile compared with other non-Apple laptop brands.

    Asus is the top non-Apple laptop option to consider for tasks, with 47.7% of CNET readers giving it high ratings. That’s followed by 40.4% of Asus laptop owners who say it has very good task performance. When it comes to tasks, 37% primarily use their Asus laptops for work, while 5% use theirs for gaming.

    Industry observers note that asus is well known for having lightweight laptops with all-day-and-night battery life and stunning display quality. Asus laptops like the Asus ROG Zephyrus G16 have a good port selection, which could be good for gaming, work or simply connecting different devices without the need for additional adapters. And the Asus Zenbook S 14 has a strong neural processing unit that contributes to its high-speed AI performance.

    Asus scores highest for its screen brightness and clarity, with over half (51%) extremely satisfied with its screen quality and brightness, while 38.6% say they’re satisfied, giving Asus an overall satisfaction rate of 90%. One common thread we noticed in Asus laptops is their OLED screens, which deliver high-resolution video and graphics. Asus laptops also combine stunning display quality with excellent performance and at surprisingly low prices for all of their features.

    For example, the Asus Zenbook 14 isn’t the highest-quality OLED we’ve seen, but it still produces clear text and graphics on a 14-inch screen, along with exceptional black levels, Elliott said. That’s still better than LCDs that many other non-MacBooks have, and could be the reason Asus owners rate it so highly in this category.

    Dell wins our readers over as a top choice for high-end laptops. One-third (33.3%) of Dell owners spent over $1,500, and of that percentage, 15.2% spent over $2,000.

    Dell’s premium laptops largely cater to business and gaming with their standout features and performance. The Alienware 16X Aurora is Dell’s midrange gaming laptop with user-replaceable RAM, a bright display and strong performance for $2,280. But if you want more gaming features, Dell has the Alienware 16 Area-51, which has even better gaming performance, upgradable RAM and three SSD slots for $2,530. And if you’re looking for a non-Mac alternative that comes close to MacBook quality and performance, the higher-end Dell XPS 14 is the one to choose. It has the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 graphics and 1TB of storage for $1,950.

    It has been revealed that CNET commissioned Alchemer to conduct the People’s Picks survey to compile data. The survey was carried out online, and all figures are from Alchemer. The total sample comprised 1,003 adults. The figures have been weighted and are representative of all US adults (aged 18 plus). Fieldwork was undertaken from Sept. 1 to Oct. 10, 2026.

    Is Lowe's a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (756 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Eric Volkman – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:47AM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that lowe's Companies (LOW +2.78%) stock enjoyed a midweek bump thanks to the third-quarter results it posted Wednesday morning.
    • The post-earnings share price pop was encouraging, although it evaporated the following day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Eric Volkman – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:47AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Lowe's Companies ›.

    Recent findings suggest that lowe's Companies (LOW +2.78%) stock enjoyed a midweek bump thanks to the third-quarter results it posted Wednesday morning. It was a beat-and-raise quarter for the durable home improvement and hardware retailer, with a near-double-digit increase in total sales. And while there was a large asterisk next to that figure, other positive developments helped lift the stock, at least initially.

    The post-earnings share price pop was encouraging, although it evaporated the following day. Here's my view on whether the shares can go higher, and meaningfully, before long.

    The quarter saw Lowe's post $22.8 billion in net sales, up an uncharacteristically high 9% year over year. At first glance, there was a mismatch between that growth figure and the comparable sales increase of 1.8%. This is due to the firm's purchase of a latest asset, wholesale construction materials distributor Foundation Building Materials (FBM), revealed in August 2025. The deal closed in October, which was too late for FBM's full third-quarter 2025 results to be consolidated into Lowe's. Since the 2026 quarter included a full three months of FBM's performance, the year-over-year comparison for Lowe's total net sales was skewed.

    Regardless, the line item exceeded the consensus analyst estimate of $22.4 billion.

    Sources indicate that as for net income, there was also a note next to both the GAAP and non-GAAP (adjusted) flavors of that number. On a GAAP basis, profitability was $1.67 billion, or just under 4% higher year over year. Translated into a per-share, adjusted figure, the improvement was barely over 1% (at $3.10). On top of that, refunds from the Trump administration tariffs that were ruled illegal put roughly $250 million in Lowe's coffers and juiced both GAAP and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) by $0.34. So what we can call organic adjusted EPS fell by almost 10%, to $2.76. The average analyst estimate for raw adjusted EPS was $2.89, and clearly, many investors were willing to ignore that refund-adjusted number and consider the raw one to be a beat.

    As management teams habitually do, Lowe's attributed its improvements to its current Total Home Strategy initiative, which was confirmed in 2020 and updated in late 2024. This is an attempt to be an all-encompassing, one-stop, omnichannel retailer for every customer, be it a person needing a tool for a small repair or a construction industry pro working on large-scale projects with a sizable budget. Total Home Strategy was a massive factor in the FBM acquisition and an earlier asset purchase in 2025, the interior surface design, distribution, and installation specialist Artisan Design Group (ADG).

    NYSE · As of 10:00 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Although the top- and bottom-line results for Lowe's were somewhat inflated, the organization was confident enough to raise key guidance items. It now expects total sales of $92.5 billion for all of 2026; that's higher, if not dramatically so, than its previous forecast of $92 billion. Comparable sales are now expected to rise by around 0.5% over the 2025 results. That provided investors some fuel for optimism, as the preceding estimate was that the key indicator would be flat.

    Lowe's maintained its adjusted EPS projection of $12.25, and its guidance for capital expenditures (up to $2.5 billion).

    In a recent development, I find it admirable that Lowe's has articulated and is executing a clear and sensible strategy for growth (even if its all-things-to-all-clients nature might prove overly ambitious). I also like the fact that it's growing, if slowly, its sales and "comps" despite lingering weakness in new housing construction in this country.

    Would that make me a buyer of its stock? To me, the jury's still out on the current iteration of the Total Home Strategy, which, like all grand initiatives, needs time to take full effect. I'd prefer to see concrete evidence that it's really boosting Lowe's results before pulling the trigger on an investment -- especially given the unspectacular third-quarter organic growth rates (or declines). So basically, I'd adopt a wait-and-see stance on the retailer's stock.

    #4301. Tech Report: Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (919 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (919 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
    • According to recent reports, A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
    • Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac problems as early as 1998.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

    According to recent reports, A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

    Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac problems as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

    Back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

    According to recent reports, an Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

    Apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and people. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

    When news of the shutdown spread, Apple owners flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

    It has been revealed that for many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

    It has been revealed that in discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community people to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others noted the site grew less helpful over the years.

    CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he said.

    Sources indicate that just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

    It has been revealed that the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push users away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

    Industry observers note that reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual customers to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

    Apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The company may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum people on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

    In a recent development, whatever the reason, the circle of Apple consumers helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

    #4299. Tech Report: Here Be Dragons: Why AI Is Not The Thing To Fear

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1061 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Here Be Dragons: Why AI Is Not The Thing To Fear

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1061 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Adrian Carr is CEO of global master data management provider Stibo Systems, which empowers companies through trustworthy intelligence.
    • ​For me, the phrase “here be dragons” conjures images of a cartographer from times of old, reaching the edge of what he knew.
    • So, even the dragons were a story told to fill a gap.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Adrian Carr is CEO of global master data management provider Stibo Systems, which empowers companies through trustworthy intelligence.

    ​For me, the phrase “here be dragons” conjures images of a cartographer from times of old, reaching the edge of what he knew. With a quill pen, he fills the empty spaces of his maps with sea serpents and other beasts. Warnings, to keep sailors from venturing too far into the unknown.

    So, even the dragons were a story told to fill a gap.

    I find that fitting, because we are doing exactly the same with AI.

    Every generation reaches the edge of its map. Ours just happens to involve AI, and the margins are filling up quickly. Some people are drawing utopias there, others monsters. Most of us draw a bit of both.

    The people who move a map’s edge are rarely the ones who draw dragons. They are the explorers, the innovators and they sailed on regardless of them. For AI to be created, it needed many things in place first: the microchip, which made processing power small and cheap enough to be everywhere. It also needed the internet, which connected us all and filled the world with the text, images and records that models learn from.

    In a recent development, each of those innovations was somebody’s edge of the map once. Ours is simply the next.

    The trouble is that most of us are frightened of this one. Humans respond to uncertainty in different ways, but most of us feel fear. With AI, we are also confused, anxious about missing out. Yet fear has never stopped all of us. There are always people who overcome it and sail on, and they are the ones who change the trajectory of the human race.

    For 20 years, search engines taught us to speak to machines in fragments. We would type “restaurants near me open now” or “weather tomorrow afternoon.” We adapted to the machine. AI has turned that around—the machine now adapts to us, answering (even badly phrased) questions in plain language and with context.

    Industry observers note that that is a real shift. But it also creates a trust paradox. A global study of more than 48,000 people by the University of Melbourne and KPMG found that 66% use AI regularly, yet only 46% trust it. More telling, 66% said they rely on AI output without evaluating its accuracy, and 56% said they had made mistakes in their work because of it.

    We use AI, we doubt AI and we act on AI anyway. That is precisely the kind of gap where dragons get drawn.

    When you began reading this, you probably assumed the dragon I was talking about was AI. If you are still with me, I believe the dragon on our map is the unexamined ground underneath AI.

    Earlier this year, I had my first journey in a car capable of autonomous driving. I confess to many nervous minutes watching every move, my head spinning to check for traffic and cyclists. And plenty of people share that unease; AAA’s 2025 survey found that 6 in 10 U.S. drivers are still afraid to ride in a self-driving vehicle.

    Sources indicate that but this feeling faded as I reasoned that the car had more sensors than me, with greater capability. The car could react faster. It was unlikely to get distracted or even sneeze. I concluded the car was likely a safer driver than I could ever be.

    In a recent development, but on that same journey, the car got stuck at a traffic light. The lights were not in the standard positions, and the car became confused. The car was capable, but the underlying infrastructure had gaps.

    Most organizations are in the same position with AI. We spend a great deal of time asking what models can do, and far less asking whether the information under them is fit for a machine to act on.

    Sources indicate that for more than a century, charts of the Coral Sea revealed Sandy Island, a sizable strip of land between Australia and New Caledonia. It was copied from map to map, eventually to digital maps. In 2012, scientists on an Australian research voyage noticed it was missing from the ship’s own nautical charts and went to have a look.

    It has been revealed that they found only an expanse of open water. No island.

    Every large organization has phantom islands of its own, and customer data is where I would look first. The same customer’s information can exist across sales, service, billing and marketing systems as several slightly different people, each version confident it is the right one. Something changes, and only some of those records get updated.

    In a recent development, for years, we smoothed over those gaps with human intervention. But an AI agent acting fast will just act on whichever version of the customer it finds first, and it will repeat the mistake as faithfully as the mapmakers copied Sandy Island.

    In a time when we are likely to jump ship due to anything less than a great customer experience, that is not good.

    Industry observers note that every dragon dissolves as the map expands. Someone asks, “Are you sure?” and goes to find out. Curiosity gets us close enough to look. Trust is what makes the dragon disappear. And trust comes from evidence, not reassurance.

    It has been revealed that AI will follow the same path. The organizations that go furthest will be the ones that get their foundations ready for machines to trust. For leaders, that means asking a different set of questions: Do we have one version of each customer that we would trust an AI agent to act on? Where is our information still designed only for human eyes? Do we know where our most vital data comes from, who owns it, how current it is and whether it is governed?

    It has been revealed that we should stop wasting energy on our fear of the unknown. We must assess the risks logically, mitigate them and step forward cautiously, because step forward we must.

    Trusted data is what turns artificial intelligence into trustworthy intelligence.

    That is how the map gets bigger.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sarah Sidlow – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:48AM EST.
    • As the digital finance landscape evolves, investors are weighing the growth potential of Robinhood Markets (HOOD -0.60%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -0.44%) to determine which firm offers a better path forward.
    • In a recent development, while Robinhood started by democratizing stock trading for retail investors, SoFi began as a student loan refinancer before becoming a diversified bank.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sarah Sidlow – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 5:48AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›.

    As the digital finance landscape evolves, investors are weighing the growth potential of Robinhood Markets (HOOD -0.60%) and SoFi Technologies (SOFI -0.44%) to determine which firm offers a better path forward.

    In a recent development, while Robinhood started by democratizing stock trading for retail investors, SoFi began as a student loan refinancer before becoming a diversified bank. Both companies now compete for the same tech-savvy consumers by offering everything from credit cards to crypto trading, creating a compelling comparison between two major fintech players.

    In its latest annual report, filed for the 2025 fiscal year, Robinhood highlighted its shift toward institutional services through the acquisition of Bitstamp. It is increasingly a major player in financial stocks by expanding its support for Bitcoin (BTC -3.67%) and other digital assets. The firm also maintains a joint venture, Rothera, to offer futures and derivatives trading for its retail and institutional owners.

    Reliable recent quarterly figures for at least one of these companies aren't available, so this comparison uses each manufacturer's latest full fiscal year. For the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, Robinhood reported nearly $4.5 billion in revenue, which reflects a 51.6% increase over the previous year. The company achieved a net income of approximately $1.9 billion, benefiting from heightened trading activity and the expansion of its subscription services.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 1.3x, which measures total debt relative to shareholder equity. The current ratio is approximately 1.3x, measuring a firm's ability to cover short-term debts with assets that can be converted to cash within a year. Robinhood also produced roughly $1.6 billion in free cash flow, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and capital expenditures.

    It has been revealed that soFi Technologies is a member-centric digital financial services organization that offers a comprehensive suite of banking, lending, and investing products. The company operates as a national bank and serves approximately 17.1 million members across its platform. It also leverages its technology segment to provide infrastructure to other fintech firms and partnered with Mastercard (MA +1.36%) to support its expanding card services.

    During the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, SoFi generated nearly $3.6 billion in revenue, representing a growth rate of approximately 35.1% compared to the prior year. The tech giant recorded a net income of roughly $481.3 million, a significant swing from its historical performance as it continues to scale its digital banking operations. This improvement highlights progress in monetizing its member base across multiple product lines, including lending and financial services.

    It has been revealed that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, SoFi carries a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.2x, indicating how much debt the manufacturer uses relative to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio is roughly 0.2x, which measures the company's ability to meet short-term liabilities with short-term assets. During the same period, the company reported a negative free cash flow of nearly $4.0 billion, representing cash from operations minus capital expenditures.

    Robinhood Markets carries risks of heavy reliance on transaction-based revenue, particularly payment for order flow, which could be impacted by changing regulatory standards. The tech giant also navigates significant litigation risks related to historical trading volatility involving stocks like GameStop (GME +0.58%). Its expansion into international markets like the European Union brings complex operational and regulatory challenges that could affect future growth.

    SoFi Technologies is exposed to risks associated with its concentration in personal loan products, which could face higher default rates during an economic downturn. As a bank holding company, it must also adhere to strict capital requirements that may limit its operational flexibility compared to non-bank rivals. The company faces intense competition from legacy institutions such as Wells Fargo (WFC +1.18%) and Citigroup (C -1.21%).

    Trading at a lower multiple of future Forward P/E estimates, SoFi Technologies appears to be the more value-oriented option for investors today.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    SoFi stock has severely underperformed Robinhood Markets over the last three years, returning about 106% to investors vs. Robinhood's blistering 754%. But despite those results, I'd choose SoFi heading into 2027. SoFi trades at a lower earnings multiple and a smaller market cap, offering a lower-priced entry for fintech investors. In its latest quarter, it reported record adjusted revenue, EBITDA, net income, members, and products used, and raised its full-year guidance. Free cash flow was still negative at -$3.12 billion, negative FCF isn't uncommon for fintechs in growth mode, as loans held for sale are often recorded as cash outflows. In Q3 2026, loan originations hit a record $16.9 billion.

    Sources indicate that soFi's product offerings were already more diverse than Robinhood's, and it now may be poised to recapture another important market: cryptocurrency. SoFi returned to crypto trading last year, allowing members to buy, sell, and hold more than 40 cryptocurrencies. It's also introduced a stablecoin, on-chain transfers, and a tokenized deposit, meaning it may be able to tap into some of Robinhood's biggest growth drivers while offering investors a broader financial services portfolio and a lower stock valuation.

    What You Can Pay for with Scholarship Money

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Scholarships are meant to pay for the cost of attendance to study at a college or university.
    • Some scholarships restrict the funds to specific costs, such as tuition.
    • Here are the most common college costs you can pay with scholarship money.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scholarships are meant to pay for the cost of attendance to study at a college or university. This often includes required bills and purchases, such as tuition, textbooks and on-campus living expenses.

    Some scholarships restrict the funds to specific costs, such as tuition. How you can apply the money may depend on the scholarship’s requirements.

    Here are the most common college costs you can pay with scholarship money.

    » MORE: Best websites for scholarships.

    Scholarships commonly pay toward the tuition and fees your college charges.

    Sources indicate that tuition usually covers only the cost to enroll in classes. Your college will also charge fees for a variety of reasons, such as attending a lab portion of a class, access to on-campus technology, facility maintenance and student activities. You’ll have to pay many of these fees regardless of if you use those facilities or participate in campus activities. Fees are often charged with tuition on the same bill so that you pay them together.

    Tuition and fees cost students at public four-year institutions an average of $32,730 for the 2026-2027 school year, according to College Board’s 2026 report. If you use scholarship money to pay for these costs upfront, it can help you save a good chunk of money.

    Sources indicate that scholarship money also pays for textbooks and supplies you need to complete your courses. These can include physical books, e-books and software licenses to access online content.

    Depending on the scholarship, the cost of additional supplies that are required for certain courses might be covered as well. For example, nursing students might have to purchase scrubs with their college’s logo or medical supplies such as stethoscopes for clinical shifts.

    Some scholarships will pay for the purchase of a laptop because you’ll likely need one to complete your coursework; however, you’ll want to confirm that the money can be used for that purchase before buying one.

    Industry observers note that your scholarship might help cover some of the costs of living on campus, including paying for a dorm room and meal intends (often called room and board). To apply the funds, you usually have to live in university housing, which might be in a dormitory or even university apartments.

    Many students can purchase meal intends to eat meals in their college and university cafeterias. These plans are usually for a set number of meals each week and might be required for first-year students. Because meal plans are part of college expenses, some scholarships will let you apply the funds to purchase a meal blueprint.

    Some scholarships might also allow money to pay for campus parking fees because those are paid directly to the college or university.

    » MORE: What is need-based financial aid for college?

    In a recent development, scholarships are generally intended only for educational expenses such as those explained above, but there are some scholarships that want you to use the money for specific expenses. If your scholarship has this type of restriction, your award letter should outline how the funds must be used, such as paying for tuition and fees only.

    If you aren’t certain whether there are restrictions on how you can spend your scholarship money and the scholarship was paid directly to your college, you can call your financial aid office to ask. But you’ll want to contact the organization that awarded you the scholarship to ask about restrictions if the scholarship money was sent to you instead.

    Even if a scholarship is open to most educational costs, expenses that are rarely allowed to be covered by a scholarship include:.

    Some transportation costs such as car payments.

    Non-essential supplies such as clothing or entertainment.

    Travel, especially unrelated to college.

    According to recent reports, scholarships can be paid directly to your college or to you, depending on the individual scholarship. If the money goes to your college, it’s applied to your account based on the scholarship’s requirements. For example, if the funds are only allowed to pay for tuition, the financial aid office will apply the money to your tuition bill to reduce how much you owe.

    According to recent reports, scholarships work the same way for room and board. If your scholarship will pay toward the costs of living on campus, the money will reduce how much you owe or cover the costs entirely so that you don’t owe anything.

    According to recent reports, in some cases, you might be able to use your scholarship money to pay for books or supplies. If that’s allowed, the funds might be available on your account through the college bookstore. Instead of paying the entire cost of your textbooks with cash or your student loans, you can pay with the scholarship money.

    If your scholarship sends you the money instead of giving it to your college, you’ll be responsible for using the funds to pay for eligible costs instead of your university automatically applying it toward your bill.

    » MORE: Strategies to pay for college.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
    • The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
    • Industry observers note that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The upcoming program expands on the organization’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which launched in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

    The pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole new influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

    Industry observers note that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

    Sources indicate that first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

    As any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

    According to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

    According to recent reports, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

    Uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

    An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

    #4289. AI Is Already Critical Infrastructure. The AI Harness Is The Part You Own

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    AI Is Already Critical Infrastructure. The AI Harness Is The Part You Own

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Pavel Bykov is the Co-Founder and CEO of IP Fabric, which has been pioneering automated network assurance since 2016.
    • Industry observers note that according to McKinsey’s latest State of AI survey, 44% of organizations that use AI say it’s now scaling across their enterprise, up from 38%.
    • Sources indicate that ​I heard a story about an insurance agency whose employees used “shadow” AI to respond to customers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Pavel Bykov is the Co-Founder and CEO of IP Fabric, which has been pioneering automated network assurance since 2016.

    Industry observers note that according to McKinsey’s latest State of AI survey, 44% of organizations that use AI say it’s now scaling across their enterprise, up from 38%. In many organizations, AI is still considered an experiment. But that doesn’t mean individual AI use hasn’t already become critical infrastructure, sometimes without leadership even realizing.

    Sources indicate that ​I heard a story about an insurance agency whose employees used “shadow” AI to respond to customers. Although that particular AI application wasn’t approved, it had already become part of the agency’s customer service workflow. If employees suddenly lost access to the model they were using, customer service would be impacted.

    As AI agents start running work on their own, such dependencies will only grow deeper. Banning AI isn’t realistic; instead, we must treat it as the business continuity concern it really is.

    It has been revealed that organizations have spent two decades learning how to manage their reliance on cloud and SaaS providers. They can measure service availability, latency and other metrics, and create backups to prepare for possible outages.

    AI introduces a less deterministic dependency. An AI service can stay online and keep returning answers after its behavior has changed. Dependent workflows can appear fine while producing less accurate or less complete results.

    It has been revealed that in June 2026, a U.S. export-control directive led Anthropic to suspend Claude Fable 5 for all customers. When it returned in July, Anthropic said its new safety classifier would flag benign coding and debugging requests more often, possibly sending blocked requests to an older model. In August, Anthropic retrained Fable 5’s separate biology classifier, which sends flagged requests to yet another model. Within two months of launch, Fable 5 had been suspended, rerouted and retuned, all under the same model name. If an organization wasn’t evaluating its outputs with Fable, it wouldn’t understand how these changes affected its work.

    Industry observers note that ​IT leaders need a proposal for what happens if a provider changes its model, performance falls below an acceptable level or prices fluctuate. Price can move in either direction; for example, in September, Anthropic noted its fresh Opus 5.5 model would cost about 40% less than its predecessor on typical workloads. If an organization doesn’t have the flexibility to switch models, it can’t take advantage of those savings.

    A business continuity strategy should start by defining an acceptable level of model performance, which can’t be left to provider benchmarks. This plan should also include a test set of problems the organization has already solved and can use to measure model performance. Present each model with a problem, withhold the known answer, and score the result. These tests should determine:.

    1. Did the AI model complete its task?

    Sources indicate that 2. Was the result checked against an authoritative source the AI did not produce?

    According to recent reports, 3. Does the model answer questions consistently, if asked multiple times?

    4. What did each completed task cost?​​.

    Run this test set any time a model changes. Without this internal baseline, an organization might sense that a service has become less reliable, but be unable to demonstrate any shift in behavior.

    ​An AI harness is often described as a layer that filters model inputs and outputs. I think about it differently: Picture a talented soccer player, alone with a ball on a planet covered in grass. His ball control is perfect, and he can run the ball around the planet endlessly. It is impressive, and it is pointless.​.

    In a recent development, ​To make this a game, you need lines, goal posts, rules, referees, a scoreboard and a stadium. A harness is all of those things for AI. It gives the model a goal and defines what a successful output is. It determines which data and systems that AI may touch. It also keeps a record that helps organizations learn, as corrections and verified reference data stay in the harness, rather than in the model itself.

    In a recent development, any soccer game requires an impartial referee. In my field, if an AI agent proposes a firewall change, then that proposed change must be checked against a model of network behavior that the agent did not build or edit. The system that validates a change should never be the system that made it.

    Sources indicate that AI harnesses also ensure business continuity throughout times of change. On any soccer team, players can get injured or transferred, but the club keeps its stadium, its rules and its record. When my firm changed its AI subscription, I had AI rebuild my workflow setup into a portable harness in a folder I control. This harness also helps me to run the same tests across several models and pick the one that fits each workflow, rather than assuming the most expensive one is best.

    You don’t need to own every data center or chip in your AI stack to stay in control, but you do need to decide which parts of the stack you own, because providers are moving the harness itself into their clouds. OpenAI’s upcoming always-on agents each live in the cloud. These agents don’t support data residency, and their cloud orchestration events don’t reach the customer’s existing telemetry collector, but when the referee, the stadium and the record all belong to the provider, the provider’s changes become yours.

    Recent findings suggest that an organization may allow hosted models and provider-run agents for low-risk work, but require business-critical workflows to adhere to rules, reference data, tests and records in systems you control, running the model privately where the data requires it. To draw these lines, organizations need visibility into how teams and applications actually use AI.

    Ultimately, organizations can’t control when a provider updates their model, but they can control the harness they put around AI. That governance is the key to keeping critical workflows running, no matter how the models underneath them may change.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Perpetual Futures Are Surging in Popularity, But They Are Also Facing Mounting Controversy. Here's What Crypto Investors Need to Know.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that perpetual futures ("perps") are coming to the U.S., and they're already a polarizing topic thanks to their availability on international crypto venues going back years.
    • In a recent development, but perps are controversial for the very same reason that they're so lucrative for these platforms to offer: Most investors lose, and the venue makes money no matter what happens along the way.
    • Recent findings suggest that A perpetual future is a financial derivative contract that tracks an asset's price and never expires for as long as it's held.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Alex Carchidi – Nov 20, 2026 at 5:50AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Robinhood Markets ›.

    Sources indicate that perpetual futures ("perps") are coming to the U.S., and they're already a polarizing topic thanks to their availability on international crypto venues going back years. Robinhood Markets (HOOD -0.60%) noted in September that it prepares to offer them to U.S. users in the coming months, with up to 10-fold leverage on Bitcoin (BTC -3.67%) and Ethereum (ETH -4.23%) perps. Coinbase Global (COIN +1.03%) won approval to list stock perps in the U.S. this month. Hyperliquid (HYPE -7.96%) made a name for itself by tailoring its decentralized exchange to the needs of crypto perps traders.

    In a recent development, but perps are controversial for the very same reason that they're so lucrative for these platforms to offer: Most investors lose, and the venue makes money no matter what happens along the way. Here's what crypto investors need to know about perpetual futures and why they will be one of the most important battlegrounds for regulators and businesses alike during the next few years.

    Recent findings suggest that A perpetual future is a financial derivative contract that tracks an asset's price and never expires for as long as it's held. They're almost always traded using leverage, or borrowed funds, which enables an investor's deposited collateral to control a far larger position than they otherwise could. And therein lie many of the factors that make perpetuals controversial.

    It has been revealed that using a fairly volatile asset like Bitcoin as an example, with $1,000 in collateral and 10-fold leverage selected, the trader controls a $10,000 Bitcoin position. Thus, a 1% move upward in Bitcoin's price yields a $100 gain for the trader. However, if Bitcoin were to fall by 10% from the starting price, the position would be zeroed out, as the loss would be equal to 100%. Aster (ASTER -2.95%), a decentralized perpetuals exchange that competes with Hyperliquid, allows up to 1,001-fold leverage on Bitcoin, so a 0.1% price move down leads to a 100% loss.

    In a recent development, exchanges usually liquidate (forcibly close) positions well before collateral hits zero. One consequence is that being right about an asset's future price is completely useless if a price dip between the present and that future leads to liquidation before the prediction plays out.

    Funding payments are automated recurring payments that keep a perp contract's price near the underlying asset's market price; when the perp's price is above the underlying asset's price, buyers pay sellers the funding payment, and vice versa.

    Hyperliquid's documents set a baseline of about 11.6% per year paid by buyers to sellers, but the actual funding rate changes with market sentiment. For that Bitcoin position worth $10,000, that's $1,160 a year in fees, more than the original stake, assuming the coin's price doesn't move. But most perpetuals positions aren't held for long enough for that to occur anyway.

    In a recent development, most individual investors lose money when they dabble in perpetuals. The natural users of perpetuals are hedge funds, market makers, and other groups that are sophisticated enough to implement complex, systematic trading strategies without falling victim to the typical pitfalls.

    It has been revealed that per some of its regulatory filings in Europe, Robinhood rates crypto perps seven out of seven for risk. According to a study this year by researchers at Stanford and Columbia universities, retail investors on Hyperliquid's exchange lost $1.1 billion from March 2025 through June 2026 by using perpetuals, whereas professional market makers brought in $208 million.

    CRYPTO · As of 9:57 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Nonetheless, perpetuals are coming to the U.S. in a big way. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) approved a Bitcoin perp on May 29, and stock perps were approved on Nov. 3.

    Some are fighting back. Two lawsuits in particular argue that perps are actually technically swaps, which would make them a separate derivative category with different rules if the courts agree.

    Sources indicate that CME Group (CME +1.55%) is suing to halt crypto perps, and another group backed by Citadel Securities is suing to stop stock perps, arguing that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) should oversee them rather than the CFTC. In opposition are Coinbase and the prediction market Kalshi, which are backing the CFTC in court. If the court sides with the challengers, stock perps could land under SEC rules that limit retail access.

    Even if they're fully legalized and available, most smart long-term investors should skip perps because they're simply far too risky for non-professionals.

    Buying the businesses or cryptocurrencies that will benefit from perp’s proliferation, like Hyperliquid and Robinhood especially, is likely the most straightforward way to get some upside from their increasing popularity.

    In a recent development, when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 790%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 202% for the S&P 500.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    11 Steps I Use for Quick Smart Home Prep for Guests and Holiday Visitors

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1188 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over.
    • If you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices.
    • Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

    If you have holiday or event intends involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

    Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

    Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

    Video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

    Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

    It has been revealed that cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

    Today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

    Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

    A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

    Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

    According to recent reports, keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be important if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

    ADT’s latest hub has a few extra tricks.

    Industry observers note that home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

    According to recent reports, you can still get key alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

    It has been revealed that A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

    Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

    It has been revealed that smart home speakers like an Echo or the latest Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

    It has been revealed that voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

    According to recent reports, for example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

    It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

    A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

    With the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

    If you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

    This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

    In a recent development, don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

    For more on protecting and utilizing your smart home, take a look at our favorite DIY home security systems, our list of the best smart home devices and our total smart home cheat sheet for all platforms.

    Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child.
    • I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
    • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

    I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

    Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

    Industry observers note that it all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

    After a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

    Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

    I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

    I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

    Getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one substantial image using multiple sheets.

    It has been revealed that since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

    But I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

    There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty quickly.

    Industry observers note that another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid indicates will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a big deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That mentioned, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

    I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

    I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

    #4283. Tech Report: I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable
