    Tech Report: I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1641 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
    • Sources indicate that take Southwest Airlines, for example.
    • According to recent reports, "Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

    Sources indicate that take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

    According to recent reports, "Experiences create lifetime memories,” notes Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

    It has been revealed that southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

    Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but substantial-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

    The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

    In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

    A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

    Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

    A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

    A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

    A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

    Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

    It has been revealed that as of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

    Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

    $1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

    Industry observers note that four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

    If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

    Sources indicate that using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

    Daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

    Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

    Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

    I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

    Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

    Again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

    Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

    It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

    I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

    Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

    It has been revealed that grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

    It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

    Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

    In a recent development, the biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

    You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

    With that said, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

    These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

    Scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

    Finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

    In a recent development, southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

    Sources indicate that but every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

    It has been revealed that personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

    Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

    "We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” says Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

    If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

    Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

    Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

    Industry observers note that you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    #4281. Breaking: Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2229 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2229 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
    • But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto.
    • According to recent reports, something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

    Microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some concerns. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

    According to recent reports, something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these complications, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

    Adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity manufacturer CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

    “This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

    One massive reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

    According to recent reports, if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

    In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

    Industry observers note that artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a massive or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

    Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should enhancement. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

    Another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

    Industry observers note that when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he mentioned, “it’s bad.”.

    In a recent development, as owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He states he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. New AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

    “You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand stated.

    It has been revealed that things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

    In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers notes CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

    “Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers said.

    Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

    “The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

    Sources indicate that AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

    The good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

    In a recent development, it still might not be enough, and Massive Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman mentioned he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

    And defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said this week at the New York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

    The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

    In a recent development, that’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

    “There’s effectively this substantial backlog of security challenges in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” stated Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity company focused on connected devices.

    It has been revealed that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

    “Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse said.

    Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of complications is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with vital, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to enhancement so frequently these days.

    “It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” mentioned Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

    Industry observers note that and patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s concerns on Tuesday.

    It has been revealed that things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents upcoming problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing issue.

    It has been revealed that in the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

    Significant Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

    “I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” stated Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

    Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy indicates.

    In a recent development, that means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into new software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

    According to recent reports, the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

    “I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he noted. “It will hurt a bit.”.

    Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more key than ever.

    “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers said. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

    Recent findings suggest that but consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a firm isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

    In a recent development, we don’t have to put up with it, Barlet says. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he noted.

    #4280. Breaking: What Biology Can Teach About Building AI

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (994 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: What Biology Can Teach About Building AI

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Zuzanna Stamirowska is the CEO & Co-Founder of Pathway, an AI lab building AI architecture that continually reasons, learns, and evolves.
    • Sources indicate that ​​​We in the AI industry have been solving an engineering problem when we should have been answering a biological one.
    • In a recent development, ​​Neuroscience may hold the answer to persistent memory and continuous learning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Zuzanna Stamirowska is the CEO & Co-Founder of Pathway, an AI lab building AI architecture that continually reasons, learns, and evolves.

    Sources indicate that ​​​We in the AI industry have been solving an engineering problem when we should have been answering a biological one. The brain has already figured out memory, so why haven’t we copied it?​.

    In a recent development, ​​Neuroscience may hold the answer to persistent memory and continuous learning. It has for millions of years. The brain has been pointing to the solution AI engineers have been chasing all along. If we model our systems after how the human brain already works, we can build AI that doesn’t need constant oversight, prompting and re-reminding.

    Sources indicate that ​The human brain runs on about 20 watts of energy. Today’s AI data centers are crossing the gigawatt threshold—that’s a billion watts, or roughly 50 million times more power than a single human brain. Compute demand is growing more than twice as fast as chip efficiency, and industry estimates project roughly $500 billion a year in CapEx just to keep pace.

    As the co-founder and CEO of Pathway, I build post-transformer architectures inspired by the brain, informed by my background in complexity science. Studying how large networks of simple components give rise to intelligent behavior convinced me that the brain’s efficiency is a design blueprint, not a curiosity.​.

    It has been revealed that the industry needs to take a harder look at brain-like AI systems, which reflect how we think, reason and act. When new information arrives in the brain, only the neurons that care about it light up, passing the signal to their neighbors rather than waking the whole network unnecessarily. Useful, repeated connections get stronger over time. This is one way that post-transformer AI can operate. ​.

    Recent findings suggest that many of today’s models take the opposite approach. They are densely activated, running vast numbers of parameters for every token regardless of what the query actually requires. That’s a large part of why inference costs scale so steeply. ​.

    The brain stores memory in the connections between neurons, not filed away separately. AI, by contrast, largely lacks persistent memory. Most tasks start as a upcoming request that can’t call back on previous information, either given to or generated by the model. ​.

    In the brain, this works through synaptic plasticity—the brain’s ability to alter the strength and number of connections between neurons—which makes long-term potentiation (LTP) possible.

    Recent findings suggest that LTP strengthens neural pathways after repeated use and, with it, comes efficiency. The future of AI architecture is pathways that strengthen with use, built into the structure from the beginning rather than bolted on afterward. ​.

    Transformer-based models today have no equivalent. Reasoning happens once, in a single forward pass. Whatever the model figures out along the way is usually discarded the moment the session ends. No mechanism lets a thought become a habit. Every insight is rediscovered from scratch, every time, at a cost that compounds with scale, rather than shrinking with it.

    Rebuilding systems with this kind of continuous, structural learning in mind is a materially different undertaking than fine-tuning a static model to behave as if it remembers.​.

    Industry observers note that the brain does not think in words first. Language is a later evolutionary layer, built on much older systems for perception, prediction and action. A thought takes shape in the brain before it is ever translated into a sentence, and most of that shaping happens in a space with no linguistic form. ​.

    Industry observers note that transformer-based models have no equivalent space to think or reason within. They express reasoning as language because it is the only medium they have. Every intermediate step has to be written out as text, fed back in and read again, which is why long reasoning chains get slower and more expensive as the problem gets harder. The model isn’t just showing the work; it is also required to produce that work verbally to accomplish it all. ​.

    Latent reasoning is the alternative: working through a problem in a continuous, internal representation, the way the brain does, and only translating the result into language at the end, if at all. That distinction separates a system that has to talk to itself to think through complex processing from one that reasons the way your prefrontal cortex might—silently, before anything must be said out loud. ​.

    Meta has begun integrating related capabilities into its Muse personal agents with models like Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full. The models feature “Active Memory” and “Active Focus,” both intended to make the agents more capable. Active Memory lets the models carry over information about the user from one conversation to another, and Active Focus lets the agent keep working on a task by trying multiple solutions when it hits an matter. Databricks has also built Agent Memory, a managed memory feature on its Agent Bricks platform.​.

    Sources indicate that functional memory and latent reasoning are necessary tools for successful agents and, therefore, successful large language models (LLMs). However, these memory systems are right now behind paywalls and still limited in their applications. AI with memory and the ability to problem-solve cannot be limited to LLMs and agents.

    By looking beyond LLMs and their transformers, the AI industry can develop a technology that truly reflects the brain. ​.

    Evolution spent hundreds of millions of years on this problem and converged on the same three answers: memory that lives in the structure itself, learning that never stops and reasoning that happens before language. The industry has spent a decade building systems that do none of those things, and building them extraordinarily well. That is the strange position the field is in. The engineering is world-class. Next, we just have to build the models to match.​​​​.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    10 stocks we like better than Firefly Aerospace ›.

    An analyst downgrade and market skepticism over a major engine contract sent Firefly Aerospace (FLY -1.15%) sliding 22.6% this week.

    According to recent reports, firefly Aerospace stock changed hands at $19.52 as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19, down 22.6% from Friday, Nov. 13's close through Thursday, Nov. 19's close, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence. Over the same period, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.06%) dropped 5.1%, and the Nasdaq-100 was down 5.1%.

    The primary driver behind the decline was market scrutiny of Firefly's recent contract structure alongside a Wall Street Zen downgrade from hold to sell. Securities filings disclosed that AST SpaceMobile (ASTS +1.37%) issued 10 million shares to Firefly as part of an intellectual property license and rocket engine supply agreement valued at over $1.3 billion. Investors grew uneasy that a substantial portion of the contract relies on customer stock rather than guaranteed cash, while management also pushed back its Alpha Flight 8 rocket launch to early 2027. The sell-off leaves the stock down 68.6% (as of the close on Thursday, Nov. 19) from its 52-week high of $62.17.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:54 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that firefly Aerospace builds small- to medium-payload launch rockets, lunar landers, and orbital spacecraft for defense agencies, satellite operators, and commercial customers. In its last reported quarter ending Sept. 30, 2026, the manufacturer generated $110.7 million in revenue, up 259.6% year over year, while posting a net loss of $94.2 million. High production costs for its rocket line continue to weigh on profitability, keeping operational execution front and center for shareholders.

    Firefly held $534.7 million in cash and short-term investments as of Sept. 30, 2026, providing liquidity to fund facility upgrades. However, taking customer stock to fund engine production exposes the business to secondary market volatility rather than securing immediate balance-sheet cash. Receiving stock instead of cash for its rocket engines shifts the AST deal from a liquidity boost to a bet on another speculative satellite maker.

    Recent findings suggest that with trailing price-to-sales (P/S) sitting at 9.4 against a $3.5 billion market capitalization, Firefly carries a valuation that demands steady operational progress. Investors will want to watch the initial flight tests for its Block II engine upgrade, right now scheduled for the first quarter of 2027, as well as the organization's next scheduled earnings report on March 18, 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that investors may have soured on Firefly stock this week after a downgrade from Wall Street Zen. Still, it's key to remember that this is solely one firm's opinion -- not an overwhelming consensus among a multitude of analysts. Therefore, investors should take it with a grain of salt.

    Secondly, the delay of the Alpha Flight 8 launch until the first quarter of 2027 may also have disappointed investors. However, it stems from a national security customer's request rather than a tech giant misstep.

    While Firefly receiving AST stock instead of cash for engine licensing is a valid concern, it should hardly be enough to disqualify Firefly stock as a potential opportunity for exposure to the burgeoning space economy. Rather, investors should continue to monitor the company’s earnings reports carefully to confirm that Firefly continues to grow revenue and narrow its net losses.

    Toronto Raptors forward RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the team announced Thursday.

    Additionally, forward Collin Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol as a precautionary measure.

    Barrett missed Wednesday's 103-99 loss to the Washington Wizards with hamstring tightness. That was the second of back-to-back games for the Raptors, who also lost to the New York Knicks on Tuesday. Barrett played 39 minutes in that game, scoring 22 points with 5 rebounds and 5 assists.

    In a recent development, however, hamstring discomfort has been an issue for Barrett in recent weeks. He has been using a stationary bike on the sideline when not on the court, in addition to during timeouts and stoppages in play, according to The Athletic's Esfandiar Baraheni.

    Murray-Boyles left Wednesday's contest during the first half after playing four minutes. The Raptors confirmed that he would not return due to illness, which has apparently been going around the team locker room. When he sustained a possible concussion is not certain.

    Barrett, 26, is Toronto's second-leading scorer this season, averaging 20.9 points with 6.4 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game. He's shooting a career-low 28% on 74 3-point attempts. Prior to sitting out Wednesday's contest, Barrett had appeared in all 14 of the Raptors' games.

    In his second season, Murray-Boyles is averaging 9.3 points, 4.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists, in addition to 1 steal and 1.1 blocks in 14 games (eight starts). He was the Raptors' 2025 first-round pick (No. 9 overall) out of South Carolina.

    Industry observers note that toronto (5-10) has lost its past six games and eight of its past 10. The Raptors at the moment rank ninth in the Eastern Conference and 16th in the NBA. They visit the Detroit Pistons (10-4) on Friday.

    #4275. What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

    What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
    • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
    • Recent findings suggest that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The significant day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

    If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

    Recent findings suggest that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

    If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, claims Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

    Non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

    NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold notes.

    While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

    Industry observers note that “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” claims Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

    Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

    According to recent reports, got some counter space and an itch for a upcoming food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

    In a recent development, “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath states. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

    Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

    While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold states.

    Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath notes.

    Industry observers note that gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

    That mentioned, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold notes.

    According to recent reports, for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, indicates consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

    You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Latest Year’s Day.

    “Major-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold notes.

    According to recent reports, many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath claims. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

    In a recent development, shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

    It has been revealed that just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath indicates. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

    One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

    Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

    Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

    Recent findings suggest that fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch notes.

    Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

    Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

    Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

    Industry observers note that let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch notes. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

    According to recent reports, check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley notes. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

    It has been revealed that use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

    #4274. Tech Report: Voice AI Benchmarks Are Not Scoreboards

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1037 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Voice AI Benchmarks Are Not Scoreboards

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sidhant Kabra is a Co-Founder of Cekura, a company that is pioneering Voice AI evals and benchmarks.
    • ​Every few days, a new voice AI model ships with a chart that puts it on top: fastest reply, lowest error rate, most human.
    • Industry observers note that as the co-founder of Cekura, a organization that tests voice agents and publishes voice AI benchmarks, my advice is to use the rank to build a shortlist, not to make the decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sidhant Kabra is a Co-Founder of Cekura, a company that is pioneering Voice AI evals and benchmarks.

    ​Every few days, a new voice AI model ships with a chart that puts it on top: fastest reply, lowest error rate, most human.

    Industry observers note that as the co-founder of Cekura, a organization that tests voice agents and publishes voice AI benchmarks, my advice is to use the rank to build a shortlist, not to make the decision. Picking the top three to five is a good starting point. Past that, in my view, the ranking is about 2% of a benchmark’s value. The other 98% is the specific finding: where an agent breaks, compared with whom and under what conditions.

    Benchmarks are experiments. Change the line quality, the caller’s accent, the workflow or how slowly a tool responds, and the order changes. Absolute numbers don’t transfer to your business. Specific gaps do.​.

    Industry observers note that start by holding the agent constant. In one public experiment, we deployed the same Medicare insurance agent on six voice platforms and ran 23 scenarios three times on each. Workflow scores ranged from 65.2% to 95.7%. Same prompt, same tools, same workflow.

    Now change what you count. One platform passed 69.6% of scenarios when we scored only whether the agent took the right actions. Once we also counted infrastructure failures, such as long silences during tool calls that left callers unable to finish, it passed 8.7%. Neither number is wrong. They answer different questions.

    Swap the language model and the story flips again. With everything else held fixed, an open-source model beat an established proprietary one on reliability (88.1% vs. 76.3%) and replied a second faster at the median. But the proprietary model won red-team safety, 100% vs. 80%. Which is “better” depends on whether your agent books haircuts or moves money.​​.

    Recent findings suggest that composite scores hide the split. We ran 70 scripted calls through each of four production voice agents in healthcare and financial services. One led its peers on 7 of 13 behaviors: It kept talking through a caller’s “mm-hm” 89% of the time, versus 31% to 40% for the others.

    In a recent development, the same agent was the slowest to stop when a caller genuinely talked over it (71% vs. 92% to 97%), and it read a value back before using it only about half the time. On the recordings: A child’s shriek masked one digit of a card number, and the agent guessed instead of asking, then sent the wrong digits to the bank’s system. A caller mentioned her mother had died three weeks earlier, and the agent went straight to the hold without empathy.

    In a recent development, none of that shows up in a single score. All of it decides whether a caller trusts the agent.

    Humans are the other baseline. We recorded experienced support agents handling 70 calls with real callers, then played the same caller lines to seven speech-to-speech models. Human agents answered in about 11 words; the models used 20 to 60. Human agents slowed down for numbers, dates and times in 16% of those stretches, and no model did so even half as often. When a cough covered one digit of a number, no model asked for it again in more than a third of calls.

    No model was human-like across the board. What separated them was which human cue each one missed. Two models were rated more human-sounding than the human agents, yet still read numbers at full speed. Another sounded written rather than spoken in 75% of its replies.​​.

    Public leaderboards are a starting point. The truest benchmark is built on the parameters you care about: the test conditions your callers face, the workflows your agent runs and the metrics your business tracks. If you have real-world examples, such as recordings of calls that went wrong, build from those first. Two things make that possible.

    Sources indicate that the first is structured test cases. Each scenario has a defined caller, a goal and an explicit expected outcome, rather than an LLM judge reading a transcript and guessing. Voice agents don’t behave the same way twice, so a scenario counts as passed only if it passes three runs in a row.

    The second is simulating the real world, not just calling an endpoint: interrupting at exact timestamps, playing background speech and hold music, dropping packets, switching languages mid-call and making tools respond slowly.

    We split that work into three tracks, because each one fails differently:.

    • Workflow: Does the agent take the right action with the right data, and confirm it before acting?

    • Infrastructure: Does the call survive latency, noise, line dropouts and slow tools without dead air?

    It has been revealed that • Red Teaming: Does the agent hold up under multi-turn pressure, where an attacker builds trust over several turns before trying a jailbreak? One-shot attacks miss most of the risk.

    A finding is only worth something if you can reproduce it, fix it and rerun the same scenario to prove the fix held.

    Before you trust a chart, ask five questions:.

    1. What was held fixed? If the prompt, model or voice changed between rows, you’re comparing configurations, not platforms.

    Industry observers note that 2. What was counted? Look for task accuracy and end-to-end completion side by side.

    It has been revealed that 3. Do the conditions match your callers? Noise, accents, holds and language switching all move rankings.

    It has been revealed that 4. How many runs? One pass on a system that behaves differently every time is an anecdote.

    It has been revealed that 5. Can you hear the failures? A recording of the exact moment an agent broke beats any composite score.​.

    Sources indicate that this month’s leader can trail next month. The insight is what lasts: This agent guesses digits under noise; that one talks over a grieving caller. That tells you what to fix before your customers find it.

    Treat every benchmark as an experiment, and read it for the gap, not the number.​​.

    Sources indicate that forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    In a recent development, after being a darling of the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution for nearly four years, Nvidia (NVDA -2.66%) has become one of Wall Street's most controversial stocks following the unexpected resignation of founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang. The firm is facing mounting uncertainty around its leadership transition as investigations involving potential ties to Chinese intelligence and questions about its extensive AI infrastructure partnerships unfold.

    These developments have shaken investor confidence, sending Nvidia shares plunging despite the company's strong financial performance. On Nov. 17, Nvidia reported earnings for its fiscal third quarter. Total revenue grew 103% year over year to $115.8 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) surged 111% to $2.68. Management also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $130 billion, implying 91% annual growth.

    According to recent reports, legendary investor Warren Buffett's investment philosophy offers a compelling framework for evaluating Nvidia amid all of this uncertainty. Throughout his career, Buffett consistently emphasized durable competitive advantages, strong business economics, and the purchase of high-quality companies at reasonable valuations. These principles suggest Nvidia could remain an attractive long-term investment despite its current challenges.

    Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

    One of Buffett's most vital investment principles is identifying companies with economic moats. These competitive advantages protect a business from rivals, allowing it to maintain market share and generate attractive returns over a long-term time horizon. Nvidia has several characteristics that make its competitive position difficult to replicate at scale.

    Perhaps its greatest advantage is the CUDA software ecosystem, which allows developers to optimize applications for Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs). CUDA has become deeply embedded in AI research and hyperscale computing infrastructure. This creates switching costs because customers considering a move to competing platforms need to modify applications, retrain developers, and validate the costs associated with latest computing environments.

    Nvidia benefits from its extensive relationships with cloud providers such as Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet, as well as hardware manufacturers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Micron Technology, and Marvell Technology.

    Recent findings suggest that this integrated approach stitches together Nvidia’s GPUs, networking equipment, software, and accelerated computing systems. This end-to-end stack makes it difficult for competitors to replicate the platform as a whole. Although Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom's custom AI accelerators pose competitive headwinds, Nvidia's full-spectrum ecosystem provides protection beyond the performance of any individual chip.

    Importantly, these advantages are not solely dependent on Huang's personal relationships. They reflect decades of engineering investments, software development, and customer adoption that will remain in place following his departure.

    Sources indicate that buffett frequently emphasizes pricing power as a defining characteristic of outstanding businesses. Companies capable of raising prices without sacrificing customer demand usually maintain competitive advantages. Nvidia's financial performance suggests its products command extraordinary economic value even as investment in data center build-outs accelerate.

    It has been revealed that during the third quarter, Nvidia generated a 74.8% gross margin. This means roughly three-quarters of its revenue remained after accounting for the direct costs of producing its products and services. That is an exceptional margin profile for a company rapidly expanding production of next-generation chip architectures.

    Nvidia's pricing power stems from the economic benefits its products provide to customers. Compute efficiency, energy consumption, and deployment speed have meaningful financial consequences for hyperscalers developing AI models and applications. Therefore, customers are willing to pay a premium for Nvidia's technology, as its performance and accompanying software can reduce overall operating costs.

    NASDAQ · As of 10:00 AM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that perhaps Buffett's most relevant investment principle involves the relationship between business quality and purchase price. In his 1989 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter, Buffett famously wrote, "It's far better to buy a wonderful tech giant at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.".

    According to recent reports, that philosophy is particularly relevant to Nvidia today. The company's record financial performance contrasts with its recent stock price decline. The question for investors is whether Nvidia's lower valuation now offers an opportunity to buy an exceptional business at a reasonable price.

    At roughly $149 per share, Nvidia trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 16 and a forward P/E ratio of 10. Those valuations are unusually modest for a business generating triple-digit revenue and profit growth. If Nvidia sustains even a portion of its current growth trajectory, today's valuation will eventually look attractive.

    Ultimately, Nvidia appears to satisfy several important criteria of Buffett's investment philosophy. While the organization's future without Huang remains uncertain, its technological advantages and financial performance provide reasons for optimism.

    For investors willing to tolerate short-term volatility and maintain a long-term investment horizon, the recent sell-off represents an opportunity to buy the dip in Nvidia stock.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    It has been revealed that investor confidence can swiftly turn to anxiety during a bear market, when a major index, such as the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.02%), falls 20% or more from recent highs. During that time, it can lead to knee-jerk investing decisions and even cause the most stoic individuals to question their decisions.

    Fortunately, even as unnerving as it is to see a portfolio start to decline in value, history offers a few vital stats to keep in mind. And it offers a roadmap to follow before a bear market even occurs.

    As difficult as it is to watch a stock price do nothing other than seemingly fall, bear markets are natural. According to Hartford Funds, since 1928, there have been 27 bear markets compared with 28 bull markets in the S&P 500.

    In bear markets, the S&P 500 lost an average of 35%, and those bear markets lasted roughly 10 months.

    The good news is that bull markets are far more meaningful and reward long-term investors. Compared to the roughly 10-month duration of a bear market, bull markets last 2.7 years. Also, while the S&P lost an average of 35% in a bear market, it gained 112% on average during a bull market.

    Additionally, some of the best days for the S&P 500 actually occurred during bear markets. From 1996 to 2025, 48% of the best days for that major index occurred during a bear market, 28% during the first two months of a bull market, and the remaining 24% during the rest of a bull market. That means missing out on stocks rebounding during a bear market can be costly.

    Looking at a hypothetical example from Hartford Funds, a $10,000 investment in the S&P 500 in 1996 would have been worth $192,167 by 2025. And the only thing an investor would have had to do was leave it alone. In comparison, just missing the 10 best days for the index during that time would have resulted in a 56% lower return of $85,490.

    Armed with that data, history indicates there's one simple move to make to protect a portfolio.

    Recent findings suggest that if bear markets tend to be shorter-lived than bull markets and some of the best investing days are during bear markets, the solution is to fill a portfolio with investments you believe in as a long-term investment. Then, you simply leave them alone.

    In a recent development, picking stocks will look different for each individual. It could be owning Dividend Kings, which have increased their dividend payouts for 50 or more consecutive years, such as Coca-Cola (KO +0.93%) and Kimberly-Clark (KMB +2.56%). It could be owning Amazon (AMZN +0.51%), a leader in cloud infrastructure with a 28% global market share as of the first quarter of 2026. Or it could be owning leaders in the global payments market, such as Visa (V +1.06%) or Mastercard (MA +1.36%).

    Again, which companies are high-conviction, long-term holdings will look different for each investor. But what everyone building a successful portfolio will have in common is that they didn't sell when things got rocky and strategy to hold those stocks for multiple years, or even a decade or longer.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Gautam Nadkarni, Chief Technologist, Distinguished Member of Technical Staff (DMTS) - Wipro Technologies.
    • In a recent development, ​An insurance client called me this year with a problem that fit no playbook they had.
    • In a recent development, the team’s first instinct was to log it as a defect, but nothing was defective.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Gautam Nadkarni, Chief Technologist, Distinguished Member of Technical Staff (DMTS) - Wipro Technologies.

    In a recent development, ​An insurance client called me this year with a problem that fit no playbook they had. Their customer-service agent passed the preproduction evaluation at 94% accuracy and went live, yet within three weeks, complaint volumes climbed, even though nobody had touched the code. What had changed was the mix of customer queries after renewal season, and on that newly introduced mix, the agent had slipped to 81%.

    In a recent development, the team’s first instinct was to log it as a defect, but nothing was defective. The agent was behaving exactly as a probabilistic system behaves, and although it had been declared done, the real work had only just begun.

    According to recent reports, most enterprises I’ve worked with this year have faced a problem like this one. The AI we’re putting into production operates on a different principle from the software our delivery models assume, and that difference is undoing how we plan, ship, pay for and own outcomes.

    Sources indicate that A deterministic system gives the same output for the same input every time. You write a specification, build to it, test against it and ship, and at the end, the work is observably done. That idea of “done” sits underneath sprint planning, RACI matrices and vendor statements of work.

    Industry observers note that A probabilistic system offers no such certainty. The same input can produce different outputs, accuracy depends on context, data freshness and whichever queries arrive that week, and all of those drift. Performance degrades without anyone modifying the code, and when it does, nothing is broken—the system is working as designed.

    Sources indicate that KPMG’s June 2026 AI Quarterly Pulse Survey found that 53% of large U.S. firms have agents deployed, and the share chaining multiple agents across a workflow doubled in a quarter, from 9% to 18%. But only 26% of them can see what their AI systems cost to run, and Deloitte researchers report that just one organization in four has put at least 40% of its pilots into production. Agents are multiplying faster than anyone can see, cost or govern them.​.

    My read on why so many stall is that the models are usually fine, but the ways of working around them aren’t.

    Industry observers note that in a deterministic world, shipping is a finish line; in a probabilistic one, it’s where the clock starts. The agent that scored 94% in preproduction isn’t the same agent at week 12 or after the next upstream model upgrade because drift is the default rather than the exception.

    Industry observers note that the AI technologies are also adapting accordingly. Microsoft’s Build 2026 pitch states it plainly: “Their behavior shifts as models upgrade, tools change, and traffic patterns evolve and most of that drift happens silently, long after the demo.” The tooling has arrived, but the operating model that would put it to use mostly hasn’t.

    Industry observers note that an agent launch should be treated as a handover from build to operate, not a milestone. Define “good” as something measured continuously, run nightly evaluations against curated input sets and watch for when the numbers move. One client summed it up: “We used to ship and forget. Now we ship and watch.”.

    Deterministic work can be scoped into stories and committed to a sprint. Probabilistic work resists that because you don’t know whether a use case will land at 95% accuracy or plateau at 70% until you’ve tested it on real data, and even then the results vary.

    Cost has the same problem, and it bit hard this year. KPMG’s global survey found that 49% of executives had scaled back agent deployments because operating costs outran the benefits. That’s what happens when a budget built around a one-time build cost meets software that meters every run, indefinitely. “Done” is dead in finance too.

    Recent findings suggest that leaders who have adapted ask for thresholds rather than point estimates. “What accuracy are we prepared to ship at, what does each run cost and what is the playbook when we drop below the line?” are better steering questions than “When will it be done?”.

    If “done” is dead, someone has to own what comes after it, which is why titles such as agent supervisor, agent QA lead and AIOps manager are appearing in enterprise org charts. Somebody needs to own the evaluation suite, be on call when accuracy wanes and decide when behavior has crossed from variation into incident.

    In a recent development, 1. Retire “done” from your AI vocabulary. Replace it with “in operation, against these thresholds, at this run cost, with this owner.” If your steering decks still treat AI delivery as a project proposal, you’re approaching it wrong.

    2. Fund the operating layer, not just the build. Evaluation, observability, cost telemetry and on-call rotations separate a pilot from a production capability. Most stalled pilots I see failed not on model quality but because nobody funded the operating layer.

    Industry observers note that 3. Name the owner. Every AI system in production needs one accountable human rather than a committee or a vendor SLA. Until ownership is named, drift is everyone’s problem, yet nobody takes responsibility.

    It has been revealed that my insurance client didn’t solve their problem with a better model. They hired an agent operations lead, built a nightly evaluation pipeline and redefined “live” to include continuous monitoring of accuracy and cost. The agent is still probabilistic, but the operating model has stopped pretending otherwise, and that, more than any model upgrade, is what production-grade AI looks like.

    Forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Buying low-cost index funds is often the best choice for everyday people who want to make money in the markets. Here's a game strategy:.

    Sources indicate that these 500 stocks are so important that even some more broadly diversified stock market index funds, like the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF, closely track their performance.     In the past five years, VOO has delivered annualized returns of about 12%, and it's delivered even stronger annualized returns of 14.8% over the past 16 years since the fund's inception in September 2010.

    NYSEMKT · As of 9:58 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that keep in mind that over the long run, since 1928, the S&P 500 has delivered an average annual return of 9.98%. It's hard to go wrong if you're a long-term investor in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF. Buying these 500 stocks lets you own the most notable companies in America at an ultra-low expense ratio of 0.03%.     Sources indicate that what if you want to branch out from the U.S. market? Not every American investor needs to invest in international stocks, but I like to.

If you want to invest in companies from countries like Japan, Taiwan, the United Kingdom, Canada, and beyond, this global ETF lets you do it at a low expense ratio of 0.05%.

    Global stocks don't always beat the U.S. -- for most of my life as an investor, the exact opposite has happened.     NASDAQ · As of 9:56 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Bond yields have recently been rising, which has some people questioning whether now is a good time to buy bonds.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
    • It has been revealed that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
    • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

    It has been revealed that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

    Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

    For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

    While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any significant moves, notes Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

    According to recent reports, that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he says. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

    Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

    If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

    For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a new policy in the health insurance marketplace.

    Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an important part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

    Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty says.

    “Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

    You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

    At the same time, it’s key to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage firm, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

    Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

    It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

    Industry observers note that “Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he indicates. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

    Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, says Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

    Industry observers note that people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she indicates.

    According to recent reports, starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine notes. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

    Doing something new also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

    All three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

    The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

    In a recent development, reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 20, 2026 at 6:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ›.

    Last month marked the start of the fifth year of the AI-fueled bull market. Investors may be thinking the artificial intelligence investment opportunity is behind us, especially amid concerns that data centers could become harder to build due to potential regulations and higher interest rates.

    In a recent development, but global spending on AI infrastructure is projected to total $2.4 trillion next year, up 53% from this year. That hardly seems like the end of an investment cycle.

    The majority of infrastructure spending goes toward semiconductors. And while there are plenty of semiconductor stocks to choose from, these three magnificent companies could help set you up for life. I'd be comfortable buying and holding these stocks for a long time.

    Industry observers note that taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -2.81%) is the largest contract chip manufacturer in the world by a wide margin. It accounted for 73% of all spending on third-party semiconductor manufacturing in the second quarter, and that share has climbed over time due to demand for the most advanced chip technology relative to older production processes.

    In a recent development, TSMC has surpassed the competition's manufacturing capabilities, and it's unlikely to look back despite good progress from Intel and Samsung. TSMC's scale gives it much more capital to reinvest in research and development and to build additional capacity to meet demand. What's more, it has tight relationships with some of its biggest customers, including Nvidia and Apple, which allow it to design next-generation chips that meet their specific needs.

    NYSE · As of 9:56 AM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, importantly, TSMC is positioned to keep growing, regardless of which semiconductor tech giant ultimately designs the most effective chips for data centers. It has a much wider moat than any single-chip designer, thanks to physical limitations that prevent competitors from quickly taking share from the world's biggest and best chip manufacturer.

    Recent findings suggest that after a recent sell-off in semiconductor stocks, investors can pick up TSMC shares at less than 23 times forward earnings estimates. Considering management's long-term outlook of 25% revenue growth and strong margins, that's an incredible price for the stock.

    It has been revealed that applied Materials (AMAT -4.14%) offers a broad portfolio of wafer fabrication equipment. When a foundry like TSMC or companies that produce their own chips, like memory chipmakers, need to expand, Applied Materials gets a call.

    Demand for new equipment is growing swiftly as capacity constraints have put pressure on chipmakers to expand. Importantly, Applied Materials is well positioned to grow its market share over time. Its broad equipment portfolio provides cross-selling opportunities.

    More recently, Applied Materials has worked closely with manufacturers to develop integrated equipment that can save precious floor space and improve output. Applied's larger revenue base also enables it to invest more in research and development and to produce better equipment.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:59 AM ET 11/20/26.

    The stock presently trades for roughly 22 times forward earnings estimates. That's despite a strong outlook for the business over the next few years. Management expects the market for wafer fabrication equipment to grow by 30% in 2027, and it's positioned to command a growing share of those sales. Combined with stock buybacks and improved margins due to scale, earnings per share can grow extremely swiftly.

    Sources indicate that broadcom (AVGO -3.69%) contains a number of businesses, including software and chip design. While its software offerings are highly competitive, its chip business is driving growth, specifically its AI chips. Broadcom specializes in custom AI accelerator chips, or what it calls XPUs. It's the company behind Alphabet's Google's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) as well as custom chips for Meta Platforms and OpenAI.

    In a recent development, broadcom's design capabilities, specifically its chip-to-chip connectivity, separate it from other chip designers and position it well to maintain its lead in XPUs. It also maintains a close relationship with TSMC, which gives it access to tight foundry supply.

    NASDAQ · As of 9:59 AM ET 11/20/26.

    Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue is growing extremely quickly, up 143% to $10.8 billion in the last quarter. That pace is accelerating, too, with expectations for 200% growth in the third quarter.     Meanwhile, Google is growing its TPU business, selling the chips to third parties as well as deploying them in Oracle's cloud. That should support sustained revenue growth for Broadcom.

    Broadcom stock trades at less than 18 times forward earnings, suggesting investors believe the stock's growth won't last.
